target.title: fix: pause hidden session catalog polling
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Hidden Control UI tabs can repeatedly call `sessions.catalog.list` at request latency after an in-flight refresh completes or the Gateway reconnects.

The existing page-activation handler respects `document.visibilityState`, but refreshes initiated by component updates and request completion bypass that check. This creates unnecessary network activity, CPU usage, and continuous Gateway logs.

Closes #110701.

## Changes

- Apply the same visibility check to every session catalog refresh entry point.
- Prevent completed requests and Gateway reconnects from restarting catalog polling while the page is hidden.
- Preserve the existing coalesced refresh when the page becomes visible again.
- Add regression coverage for in-flight completion and reconnect behavior while hidden.

## Evidence

- Reproduced the request loop with the Control UI hidden during catalog refresh and Gateway restart.
- Confirmed the hidden page remains idle after an in-flight request completes.
- Confirmed a reconnect while hidden does not restart polling.
- Confirmed returning to the page triggers one coalesced refresh.
- Added focused regression tests for both hidden-page failure paths.

target.title: fix(sandbox): make stat output locale independent
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #106576.

Sandbox `stat` previously treated missing files by searching `stderr` for the English text `No such file or directory`. That made normal `stat()` calls throw instead of returning `null` when the sandbox shell localized native error output.

## Why This Change Was Made

This moves the `stat` contract away from localized shell text:

- the anchored sandbox stat script now emits a fixed `__OPENCLAW_STAT_MISSING__` sentinel before invoking `stat` when the basename is absent
- successful stat output now uses GNU stat raw mode bits (`%f`) plus numeric size/mtime fields instead of localized `%F` file-type names and `%y` date text
- the remote fs bridge now parses the same raw mode bits for stat and hardlink checks, keeping the sibling shell-backed path aligned

Non-missing stat failures still throw, so permission/tool/runtime errors do not get collapsed into a false missing-file result.

## User Impact

Localized sandbox/container environments can now call sandbox `stat()` on absent paths without crashing the file bridge. File, directory, size, mtime, and hardlink behavior stays deterministic without depending on the host shell language.

## Evidence

- `git rev-parse HEAD` → `79ade3501bb804e33127d2b6b2ee5fe01c601a62`
- `git diff --check` → (no output)
- Focused e2e test pass:
  ```
  $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts src/agents/sandbox/fs-bridge.backend.e2e.test.ts -t "returns null when an anchored stat parent disappears before cd"
  ```

- Test name: `returns null when an anchored stat parent disappears before cd`
  - This e2e test proves that when the anchored stat parent directory is deleted between `readlink -f` resolution and `cd -- "$1"` execution, the stat returns `null` instead of throwing.

target.title: fix(sessions): preserve full agent ID with colon in session key
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a session key contains multiple colons (e.g. `agent:my-agent:explicit:session123`), `.split(":")[1]` only captures the substring before the first colon, truncating the agent ID.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `row.key.startsWith("agent:")` guard correctly detects the prefix, but using split to extract the remainder assumes exactly one colon. Using `.slice("agent:".length)` preserves the full ID after the prefix.

## User Impact

Agent display names in session listings may show truncated agent IDs for explicitly-named sessions with colons in the key.

## Evidence

Before:
```
node -e "console.log('agent:my-agent:extra:session123'.split(':')[1])"
→ "my-agent" (truncated)
```

After:
```
node -e "const key = 'agent:my-agent:extra:session123'; console.log(key.startsWith('agent:') ? key.slice('agent:'.length) : undefined)"
→ "my-agent:extra:session123" (preserved)
```

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations

target.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)
target.body:
Closes #97750

## What Problem This Solves

Some deployments serve a Claude/MiniMax model through a proxy that intermittently degrades a native `tool_use` block into plain text. In that degraded case the tool call arrives as the namespaced/bare XML attribute dialect — `<invoke name="tool"><parameter name="x">v</parameter></invoke>`, optionally wrapped in `<function_calls>...</function_calls>` and optionally prefixed with `antml:` or `mm:`.

On current `main` two gaps remained:

1. The visible-text sanitizer recognized the `antml:` prefix but not the `mm:` prefix, so a degraded `mm:invoke` block leaked verbatim into the user-visible reply.
2. The persist-path stripper (`packages/tool-call-repair` `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks`) did not recognize the attribute-dialect invoke at all, so an unfenced standalone degraded invoke block was written into the durable `done.message` instead of being scrubbed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The degraded tool call should never reach the user, and it must not be persisted into session state either — but a legitimate code example of the same markup (inside a fenced or inline code span) must be preserved, not deleted. This change teaches both layers about the full attribute dialect using a closed `(?:antml:|mm:)?` namespace allow-list, so arbitrary `ns:` tokens in prose are never matched.

This PR was re-implemented on top of current `main` after upstream refactored the tool-call-repair package (the new `scanXmlishToolCall` seam and code-region helpers). The change is scoped to the net delta that still reproduces on `main`:

- **Visible text** (`assistant-visible-text.ts`): mirror the existing `antml:` handling for the `mm:` namespace in the tag-name scan, quick-check, and payload-start patterns. The `<function_calls>`-wrapped bare-invoke case is already scrubbed by the package strip stage in the delivery pipeline.
- **Persist path** (`packages/tool-call-repair`): a dedicated linear scanner recognizes a complete standalone invoke block (bare/`antml:`/`mm:`, `<function_calls>` wrapper, self-closing, and zero-parameter forms). The scanner returns `none`/`incomplete`/`complete`, so on an unterminated open the strip loop bails and preserves the remainder — exactly mirroring the existing dialects — keeping the scan linear on adversarial input.
- **Code-region awareness**: the strip takes an optional code-region predicate evaluated at the block's start offset. Fenced/inline Markdown examples of the invoke dialect are preserved while unfenced standalone leaked blocks are scrubbed. Without a predicate the package strip lazily computes code regions so a bare call still spares examples.
- **Plugin SDK contract preserved**: the exported `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` stays strict by default (it forces a scrub of every region, even inside code, for untrusted callers), with code-aware behavior available only via the explicit `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }` opt-in.
- **Layering**: `findCodeRegions`/`isInsideCode`/`CodeRegion` were moved into `normalization-core` (the package's only dependency) so `tool-call-repair` can share one implementation without importing app source; `src/shared/text/code-regions.ts` re-exports them so existing callers are unaffected.

Non-goals/boundaries: the native Anthropic/DSML transports are untouched; no runtime fallback execution from sanitized text is introduced; the equals dialect (`<function=...>`/`<parameter=...>`), bracket, and Harmony paths are unchanged; the invoke dialect is recognized only by the strip/sanitize paths (never promoted to an executable call and never wired into the stream-buffering scanner).

## User Impact

Users on proxied Claude/MiniMax routes no longer see raw namespaced/bare `invoke` tool-call XML in their replies, and the leaked block is no longer written into the persisted message (no session-state content loss). Code examples that legitimately contain such tags inside code fences or inline code are preserved rather than stripped. A resolved-review audit also removed an O(n²) worst case on the persist strip path, so adversarial degraded text cannot cause pathological CPU use.

## Evidence

Focused regression tests were added at the layers that own the contract:
- `packages/tool-call-repair/src/payload.test.ts`: invoke-dialect variants (bare/`antml:`/`mm:`, `function_calls` wrapper, self-closing, zero-param), code-region preservation vs. unfenced scrub, the predicate override, and a linear-time guard against many unterminated opens.
- `src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload.test.ts`: the `preserveCodeRegions` opt-in and strict default.
- `src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.test.ts`: the `mm:invoke`/`mm:parameter` visible-text case (parallel to the existing `antml:` case), alongside existing standalone-vs-inline `function_calls` delivery-path coverage.

Real-behavior proof (before = current `main`, after = this branch), driving the actual `sanitizeAssistantVisibleText` and `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` on the leak shapes:

```
=== BEFORE (main) ===
A2 mm-visible       => "Working on it.\n<mm:invoke name=\"get_weather\">\n<mm:parameter name=\"city\">Paris</mm:parameter>\n</mm:invoke>"
A3 bare-fc-visible  => "Done.\n<function_calls>\n<invoke name=\"get_weather\">\n<parameter name=\"city\">Paris</parameter>\n</invoke>\n</function_calls>"
C1 persist-unfenced => "Here you go.\n<invoke name=\"get_weather\">\n<parameter name=\"city\">Paris</parameter>\n</invoke>"
B1 persist-fenced   => "...```xml\n<invoke ...>...\n```..."   (preserved)
B2 persist-inline   => "Use the `<invoke name=\"get_weather\">` opener to start."   (preserved)

=== AFTER (this branch) ===
A2 mm-visible       => "Working on it."
A3 bare-fc-visible  => "Done."
C1 persist-unfenced => "Here you go.\n"
B1 persist-fenced   => "...```xml\n<invoke ...>...\n```..."   (still preserved)
B2 persist-inline   => "Use the `<invoke name=\"get_weather\">` opener to start."   (still preserved)
```

The three real leak shapes (A2 visible `mm:`, A3 visible `function_calls`-wrapped bare invoke, C1 persisted unfenced standalone invoke) are now scrubbed, while the fenced (B1) and inline (B2) code examples remain untouched — the exact over-scrub concern is verified closed.

O(n²) audit fix: a resolved-review pass measured the persist strip degrading quadratically on adversarial input with many unterminated invoke opens (720 KB ≈ 977 ms, scaling to seconds for a few MB). Making the scanner bail on `incomplete` (mirroring the existing unterminated-candidate bail) brought the same 720 KB input to ≈ 0.8 ms and restored linear scaling; a regression test locks this.

Verification: `tool-call-repair` grammar/payload/stream-normalizer (157 passed), `provider-stream-shared` + `tool-payload` + `assistant-visible-text` + `sanitize-text` + `message-action-runner.send-validation` + `embedded-agent-utils` (all green), `tsgo:core` and `tsgo:core:test` exit 0, `plugin-sdk:api:check` and `plugin-sdk:surface:check` exit 0 (surface budget bumped by the one new `StripPlainTextToolCallOptions` type), oxfmt clean, `git diff --check` clean. Rebased onto current `main` (`9b823c61`).

target.title: fix(codex): MEMORY.md silently truncated when memory plugin exposes only memory_recall
target.body:
Fixes #110665

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running Codex-runtime agents backed by a `memory_recall`-only memory plugin (e.g. memory-lancedb) would have their root `MEMORY.md` silently truncated at runtime instead of being routed through the memory tool. The agent appeared to start normally but lost access to the durable memory contents that exceeded the bounded-injection budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

`CODEX_MEMORY_TOOL_NAMES` in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-context.ts:48` contained only `["memory_search", "memory_get"]`. The memory-lancedb plugin registers a tool named `memory_recall` — not either of those names — so `getCodexWorkspaceMemoryToolNames` returned `[]` on such installations, `memoryToolsAvailable` was `false`, and `MEMORY.md` fell into the bounded-injection path where it could be truncated.

The fix adds `"memory_recall"` to the set (one line). `memory_recall` is a first-class recall tool: it appears in `extensions/memory-lancedb/index.ts` and is listed as the sole tool in `LANCEDB_ACTIVE_MEMORY_TOOLS_ALLOW` (`extensions/active-memory/types.ts:31`). Its omission from `CODEX_MEMORY_TOOL_NAMES` was an oversight, not a design choice.

The `doctor --lint bootstrap-size` check (issue ask #2) is **not** addressed here. Making that check runtime/harness-aware requires importing Codex extension logic into core or duplicating classification there — a cross-package change that warrants its own PR. A follow-up issue is recommended if maintainers want that diagnostic accuracy improvement tracked separately.

## User Impact

Agents using memory-lancedb (or any plugin that exposes `memory_recall` instead of `memory_search`/`memory_get`) will now have their root `MEMORY.md` correctly routed through the memory tool. The file will no longer be injected as bounded context and will not be truncated. Installations that do not expose `memory_recall` are unaffected.

## Evidence

**Failing before the fix** (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-context.test.ts`):

```
FAIL extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-context.test.ts
  Codex app-server attempt context
    × treats memory_recall as a Codex workspace memory tool
      AssertionError: expected [] to include 'memory_recall'
    × routes MEMORY.md through tools when only memory_recall is exposed
      AssertionError: expected false to be true
        → context.memoryToolRouted
  5 pre-existing tests passed
```

**Passing after the fix:**

```
PASS extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-context.test.ts
  Codex app-server attempt context
    ✓ treats memory_recall as a Codex workspace memory tool
    ✓ routes MEMORY.md through tools when only memory_recall is exposed
    ✓ ... (5 pre-existing tests)
  7/7 pass  EXIT=0
```

Only the scoped vitest file was run locally. Full CI is expected to catch any regressions in `run-attempt.test.ts` or snapshot fixtures.

---

This fix was developed with AI assistance (Claude Code) as part of a supervised bug-fix pipeline. The root-cause analysis, diff, and test evidence were independently reviewed (adversarial pass confirmed no other reference to `CODEX_MEMORY_TOOL_NAMES` exists, no snapshot hardcodes the set, and `run-attempt.test.ts` fixtures are unaffected) before this PR was submitted. Please review with the same scrutiny as any external contribution — and feel free to close if this doesn't fit the project's direction.

target.title: fix(agents): race in-flight tool promises against run abort (#103905)
target.body:
## Summary

Refs #103905 (second sub-issue only: in-flight tool promises completing into a dead run).

When stuck-session recovery aborts an embedded run, `wrapToolWithAbortSignal` forwarded the combined abort signal into the tool's `execute` but never raced the returned promise against that signal. A long-running tool handler that does not itself observe the signal kept executing after the abort and eventually delivered its result into a run that no longer existed, with nothing consuming it.

This PR makes the wrapped `execute` reject with `AbortError` as soon as the run aborts. The first sub-issue from #103905 (the abort surfacing nothing to the user: `surface_error` with `reason=none` plus draft deletion) is intentionally **not** addressed here.

## Root cause

`wrapToolWithAbortSignal` (`src/agents/agent-tools.abort.ts`) checked `combinedSignal.aborted` once before invoking the tool and then did `return await execute(...)` with no race. For a tool whose handler ignores the signal, nothing ever settled that `await` when the run aborted, so the tool promise completed later — external side effects and all — into a dead run.

## Fix

Race the tool's execute promise against the combined abort signal in a small local `raceWithAbortSignal` helper:

- When the combined signal aborts, the wrapped call rejects immediately with the existing `createAbortError("Aborted")` (same error shape as the pre-invocation abort path).
- Cancellation contract (documented in the code comment): JavaScript cannot cancel a running promise, so a tool that ignores the signal keeps executing in the background; the race only detaches its late settlement so the result never lands in the aborted run. Late tool rejections stay handled (no unhandled rejections).
- Tool-side semantics are unchanged: the combined signal is still passed into `execute`, and while the run is alive, tool results and tool errors pass through with identity (no wrapping/normalization).

The existing `abortable()` helper in `embedded-agent-runner/run/abortable.ts` was deliberately not reused: it tags abort errors for provider-retry handling in `model-fallback.ts` and normalizes non-Error rejections, both of which would change tool error semantics.

## Regression test

New `src/agents/agent-tools.abort.test.ts` (7 tests, real `AbortController` + controllable promises, no fake timers):

- Never-settling tool promise + run abort → wrapped `execute` rejects immediately with `AbortError` (previously this `await` hung forever).
- Per-call signal abort propagates through the `AbortSignal.any` combined signal and rejects the same way.
- Tool resolving after the abort → its result never surfaces from the wrapped call.
- Tool rejecting after the abort → no unhandled rejection.
- Not aborted → result passes through with identity; tool error passes through with identity; already-aborted signal still throws before invoking the tool.

## Evidence

Exact head: `3c45e700d0a76308b4848c8aa23312ce18c5855b`, based on upstream/main `40793e6f8b5d9362e9b94d9e18cd95581c6bfc18` (freshness re-verified right before push: latest main still has the un-raced `return await execute(...)` at `src/agents/agent-tools.abort.ts:35`).

Node v24.18.0, real terminal output:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/agent-tools.abort.test.ts src/agents/tool-search.test.ts src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.integration.e2e.test.ts
 ✓ |agents| src/agents/agent-tools.abort.test.ts (7 tests) 26ms
 ✓ |agents| src/agents/tool-search.test.ts (70 tests) 1716ms
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  77 passed (77)

 Test Files  1 passed (1)

[test] passed 2 Vitest shards in 7.54s
```

- `oxlint` on both files: 0 warnings, 0 errors; `oxfmt --check`: clean; `git diff --check`: clean.
- `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json` (production) and `tsgo -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents.json` (tests): both exit 0 with no diagnostics.

## What was not tested

No full gateway + plugin end-to-end run (real stuck-session recovery firing `abort_embedded_run` against a live 20-minute plugin tool over a channel): that requires a running gateway deployment with a connected channel and a multi-minute wait, which is not reproducible in this environment. target.title: fix(boot-echo): keep echo guard chunking UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The boot echo guard's 80-char sliding-window chunking uses `.slice()` on UTF-16 code-unit boundaries, which can split surrogate pairs and produce misaligned chunks near emoji/CJK characters.

## Why This Change Was Made

Surrogate pairs split by raw code-unit slicing produce orphaned high/low surrogates in the chunk set, potentially causing echo matching to misalign near supplementary-plane characters.

## Code Change

The original `sliceUtf16SafeMinLen` retried only +1 extra character when `sliceUtf16Safe` trimmed the end for a surrogate pair. But `sliceUtf16Safe` can trim up to 1 char from the start (low-surrogate skip) and up to 1 from the end (high-surrogate skip), so the range may need extending by up to 2 to guarantee the minimum window length. The fix retries up to +2.

## User Impact

Users whose prompts contain emoji or CJK characters near an echo-match boundary may see incorrect echo detection behavior.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(meeting-bot): keep local audio diagnostics readable across chunks
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators could see corrupted or fragmented local meeting audio diagnostics when a subprocess emitted non-ASCII stderr text across stream chunk boundaries. The output, input, and optional barge-in commands could each log replacement characters or partial lines.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each local audio stderr stream now owns an incremental UTF-8 decoder and bounded incomplete-line carry. Complete LF/CR/CRLF lines are logged once even when CRLF is split across chunks, an unterminated final line is flushed when the stream ends, and stderr remains drained without decoding when the logger has no debug callback; command execution, audio data flow, and logger APIs are unchanged.

## User Impact

Google Meet and Teams Meetings local audio diagnostics remain readable and line-aligned even when child-process pipe reads split a multibyte character or diagnostic line.

## What Is Intentionally Out of Scope

The separate `chrome-node` host path does not route subprocess diagnostics through this logger or perform the affected per-chunk string decoding. Its pre-existing stderr-consumption behavior is therefore separate reliability work and is intentionally unchanged by this focused decoding fix.

## Evidence

- Regression test: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/meeting-bot/realtime-local-audio-transport.test.ts` — 1 file, 2 tests passed. The tests fragment UTF-8 and newline boundaries for output, input, and barge-in stderr; verify split-CRLF framing and stream-end tail flushing; and cover bare-CR progress, UTF-8-safe 8 KiB carry bounds, and absent-debug stderr draining.
- Targeted lint: `oxlint --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/meeting-bot/realtime-local-audio-transport.ts src/meeting-bot/realtime-local-audio-transport.test.ts` — passed.
- Diff hygiene: `git diff --check` — passed.
- Real subprocess proof: the production `createLocalMeetingRealtimeAudioTransport` spawned three Node child processes. Each stderr stream delivered five chunks beginning with a single byte inside a Chinese character; all six expected diagnostic lines were logged intact and `replacement_character_present` was `false`.
- The broader local changed-check reached core typecheck but the pinned base snapshot lacked an unrelated `fs` import in `src/security/audit-extra.async.ts`. Current `main` already fixes that baseline error in #110589; no security files are changed here.

target.title: fix(xai): bound stalled generated video download body reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a gap where xAI generated-video downloads had no download-owned chunk-idle timeout on the success body reader. A mid-body stall only surfaced as a generic guarded-fetch `request timed out` (or waited the full request budget) instead of a clear download idle failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

At `downloadXaiVideo`, pass a `chunkTimeoutMs` (half the resolved request budget) + `onIdleTimeout` into `readResponseWithLimit`. The chunk-idle budget is shorter than the guarded-request deadline, so a mid-body stall produces the download-owned idle error before the generic request timeout. A continuously dripping CDN body resets the idle on every chunk and still hits the guarded request deadline.

`fetchWithSsrFGuard` already keeps its abort until `release()`, so a continuously dripping CDN body cannot hang forever on this path; the idle bound is the missing download-owned stall signal. Shared fetch/assert helpers are unchanged.

Non-overlapping: #108982 is a multi-provider video download batch and does not include xAI. #108796 is TTS WebSocket handshake tests only.

Collision check: no open hang-class PR on `downloadXaiVideo` / `extensions/xai/video-generation-transport.ts`.

## User Impact

Stalled xAI generated-video downloads fail with `xAI generated video download stalled after <timeout>ms` instead of only a generic request timeout. Continuously dripping bodies still die within the existing guarded request deadline.

## Evidence

Exact head: `c061e466764`
`oxfmt --check extensions/xai/video-generation-transport.ts extensions/xai/video-generation-transport.download.loopback.test.ts` — passed.
`git diff --check` — clean.

### Tests

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/xai/video-generation-transport.download.loopback.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```
 ✓ rejects a stalled body with the download-owned idle timeout 1441ms
 ✓ rejects a continuously dripping CDN body within the guarded request deadline 335ms
 ✓ does not bound a dripping body when only chunk idle timeout is used 412ms
 ✓ rejects a stalled body with the idle deadline before the guarded request deadline in an unmocked loopback 228ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
```

### Loopback proof

- **Stalled body (mocked guard)**: mock fetch, real `readResponseWithLimit` with `chunkTimeoutMs: 25` — rejects with `"xAI generated video download stalled after 25ms"` in 1441ms.
- **Drip body (unmocked)**: real `http.createServer` + real `fetch` + real `downloadXaiVideo` with `allowPrivateNetwork`, continuous 20ms drip — rejects via guarded request deadline.
- **Negative control**: idle-only `chunkTimeoutMs: 100` on a 20ms drip stays unsettled past 400ms.
- **Unmocked stall proof (new)**: real `http.createServer` sends initial bytes then stalls; `totalTimeoutMs: 300`, `idleTimeoutMs: 150` — idle error fires at ~150ms, well before the 300ms guard; `elapsedMs < totalTimeoutMs - 50` proves idle beat the guard.

### Not tested

Live xAI CDN against real provider endpoints — requires real API credentials.

target.title: fix(gateway): keep channels responsive after startup requests finish
target.body:
Closes #110697

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where channels started or restarted from a short-lived gateway transaction could stop accepting later work after that transaction finished. Provider callbacks, approval handlers, and automatic restarts could retain the released request's admission context and fail with `GatewayDrainingError` even though the process-global gateway fence was open.

## Why This Change Was Made

The channel manager now uses the existing process-lifetime admission boundary when it creates approval-bootstrap work, the provider task, and the tracked cleanup/recovery/restart reaction chain. Keeping the boundary in the lifecycle owner covers RPC starts, startup, health recovery, hot reload, and future callers without weakening real restart or suspension fences.

The change builds on current `main`: recent SecretRef owner isolation, gateway-native approval context, plugin HTTP route registry, stop-timeout recovery, terminal-disconnect handling, and restart accounting remain unchanged.

## User Impact

Long-running channel accounts remain responsive after the request or reload transaction that started them has completed. Real process restart and suspension still close admission normally.

## Evidence

- RED on current `main` before the fix: the three focused lifecycle cases failed with provider `true` vs `false`, approval `true` vs `false`, and automatic restart `[false, true]` vs `[false, false]`.

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

## What Problem This Solves

Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading, caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, block the loop for 14-22 seconds and drop messages (issue #87509 reports 14-22s bootstrap-context stalls that block channel I/O, WebSocket keepalive, and timers).

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

## Why This Change Was Made

Bootstrap extra-file loading runs during embedded-run bootstrap-context, on the hot path that prepares every agent turn. On `main` the exported loader reaches Node `fs.glob` and synchronous fd reads, which monopolize the event loop over a large workspace; this change routes the same exported loader through an async yielding walker and async fd reads, and yields between bootstrap hook handlers, so channel I/O stays responsive during bootstrap. The public plugin SDK surface is deliberately unchanged.

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Preserve `fs.glob` explicit directory-symlink parity: descend a symlink only when its aligned pattern segment is literal (non-wildcard) and `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace root, so an explicit configured pattern like `linked/**/AGENTS.md` still reaches descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink. Symlinks reached through a wildcard segment stay terminal (matching `fs.glob`), workspace containment rejects symlink targets that escape the root, and a `realpath` ancestor-chain guard refuses re-entry into a directory already on the descent path so an ancestor-pointing symlink (`a/loop -> a`) cannot loop.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — explicit directory-symlink glob parity across three states (real `fs.symlink`): a literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

## User Impact

Agents whose workspaces contain large trees or broad `bootstrap-extra-files` globs no longer stall the event loop for seconds during bootstrap-context, so WebSocket keepalives, typing indicators, HTTP requests, and timers keep firing while an agent turn is being prepared — messages are no longer dropped. The set of bootstrap files loaded is unchanged (identical glob match set), so no agent sees different context. Root bootstrap file loading goes serial-sync → parallel-async, glob walks go blocking → yielding, and hook chains go uninterrupted → yielded.

## Evidence

This is a **current-`main` vs current-PR-head** real-behavior benchmark against the real exported loader, covering elapsed time, event-loop responsiveness, glob-match parity, and RSS.

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces (issue #87509). This change replaces the native `fs.glob` walk with an async walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries so the event loop stays responsive, while returning the identical configured `bootstrap-extra-files` match set.
- **Real environment tested**: OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFilesWithDiagnostics` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. `main` = `9b823c610816` (native `fs.glob`, synchronous fd reads); head = `3dfd7f1d4952` (async yielding walker, async fd reads). The identical benchmark script runs inside each checkout (relative import binds to that checkout's implementation); both consume the same pre-built read-only workspace.
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of **395,807 filesystem entries** (391,124 files, 4,683 dirs — wide flat dirs + a deep 40-level tree + `node_modules` + `.git` + `.hidden` noise), with `AGENTS.md` planted at several depths (root, deep-past-old-cutoff, `.hidden/`, `node_modules/`). Configured pattern `**/AGENTS.md`. During the load a 5ms repeating timer counts liveness ticks, `perf_hooks.monitorEventLoopDelay({resolution:5})` records event-loop delay, and `process.memoryUsage().rss` is captured before/after with `global.gc()`. 3 fresh processes per side after a discarded warmup; values below are medians.
- **Failing proof before fix** (current `main` `9b823c610816`, native `fs.glob`):
  ```
  elapsed: 834.5ms
  maxEventLoopDelay: 55.5ms   meanEventLoopDelay: 8.50ms   p99: 54.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 95 / 166 expected (57.2% kept)
  rssDelta: 358.3 MB
  matched bootstrap files returned: 3
  RESULT: fs.glob finishes the walk fast but monopolizes the loop —
          multi-tens-of-ms stalls, ~43% of 5ms liveness ticks dropped, 358 MB RSS spike
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch** (identical script both sides; full reproduce recipe below):
  ```
  # build the shared 395,807-entry workspace once, then run each side from its own checkout
  node --import tsx/esm --expose-gc ./bench-bootstrap.mts run "$BENCH/ws"
  ```
- **Evidence after fix** (current PR head `3dfd7f1d4952`, async yielding walker):
  ```
  elapsed: 1244.8ms
  maxEventLoopDelay: 10.7ms   meanEventLoopDelay: 5.09ms   p99: 6.6ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 245 / 248 expected (98.8% kept)
  rssDelta: 57.0 MB
  matched bootstrap files returned: 3
  RESULT: yielding walker keeps the loop responsive — max delay near the 5ms floor,
          98.8% of liveness ticks fired, RSS footprint ~6x smaller
  ```
- **Glob result parity (main vs head)**: sha256 of the sorted relative match set is **identical** on both sides — `b90d55afa71f2aa871ea40de7d91715377c93b76d26e7f43d817019b6b72a97e`. Matched set both sides: `AGENTS.md`, the deep 40-level `deep/.../AGENTS.md`, and `node_modules/pkg000/AGENTS.md`; `.git` and `.hidden/AGENTS.md` correctly excluded by both. The custom walker changes event-loop behavior and memory, not the returned file set.

  | metric (median of 3, 395,807 entries, Node v24.10.0) | main `9b823c610816` | head `3dfd7f1d4952` |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | elapsed (ms) | 834.5 | 1244.8 |
  | max event-loop delay (ms) | 55.5 | 10.7 |
  | mean event-loop delay (ms) | 8.50 | 5.09 |
  | liveness ticks kept | 57.2% | 98.8% |
  | RSS delta (MB) | 358.3 | 57.0 |
  | `**/AGENTS.md` matches returned | 3 | 3 (identical set) |

- **Observed result after fix**: the fix trades a modest wall-clock increase (834ms → 1245ms) for the property the issue actually needs — the event loop stops stalling. Max event-loop delay drops from 55.5ms to 10.7ms (near the 5ms probe floor), liveness-tick retention rises from 57.2% to 98.8%, and peak RSS is ~6x smaller (358MB → 57MB) because the walker no longer buffers the whole `fs.glob` result eagerly. The returned match set is byte-identical (same sha256), so existing `bootstrap-extra-files` configs load the same files. At the field-report scale (much larger real workspaces), `main`'s blocking walk is what produces the 14-22s embedded_run stalls; this benchmark demonstrates the direction and mechanism (blocking `fs.glob` vs cooperative yielding) at 395,807 entries on a single dev box.
- **Reproduce**:
  ```bash
  BENCH=/tmp/bench-89040
  PR=<pr-head-checkout>
  git -C "$PR" worktree add --detach "$BENCH/main-wt" 9b823c610816   # current upstream/main
  ln -s "$PR/node_modules" "$BENCH/main-wt/node_modules"             # read-only bench, first-party deps
  cp "$BENCH/bench-bootstrap.mts" "$PR/bench-bootstrap.mts"
  cp "$BENCH/bench-bootstrap.mts" "$BENCH/main-wt/bench-bootstrap.mts"
  # build the shared workspace once (reused by both sides, walk mutates nothing)
  (cd "$PR" && node --import tsx/esm "$BENCH/bench-bootstrap.mts" build "$BENCH/ws" 400000)
  # 3 fresh processes per side, run from inside each checkout so the relative import binds
  (cd "$PR"            && node --import tsx/esm --expose-gc ./bench-bootstrap.mts run "$BENCH/ws")
  (cd "$BENCH/main-wt" && node --import tsx/esm --expose-gc ./bench-bootstrap.mts run "$BENCH/ws")
  ```
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real exported glob-resolution path (`loadExtraBootstrapFilesWithDiagnostics`) and event-loop instrumentation directly rather than through a connected channel. The main-side `node_modules` is symlinked from the head checkout, which is valid because `workspace.ts`'s transitive imports are first-party and the run is read-only. Focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

### Directory-symlink glob parity proof

- **Behavior addressed**: The cooperative walker only descended `Dirent.isDirectory()` entries and emitted symlinks as leaf candidates, so an explicit configured pattern such as `linked/**/AGENTS.md` no longer reached descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink — Node's `fs.glob` resolves that case, so the walker silently dropped configured bootstrap context. The walker now descends a literal-named path-segment symlink when `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace, keeps wildcard-reached symlinks terminal, and guards against ancestor cycles.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`. Three regression tests build real temp directories with real `fs.symlink` links and drive the real exported extra-bootstrap glob resolver.
- **Steps run**: `npx vitest run src/agents/workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts src/agents/workspace.test.ts`
- **Observed result**: `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 156 passed (156)`. The three symlink states are covered: (a) literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; (b) a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; (c) an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping (guarded by a 15s timeout). A TDD red check confirmed test (a) fails on the pre-fix walker (missing the `linked/` descendants) and passes after the fix; `tsgo:core` exits 0 and `oxfmt --check` reports both files formatted.
- **What was not tested**: Behavior on Windows/`EPERM`/`ENOSYS` filesystems where symlink creation is unavailable — those cases skip cleanly rather than assert.

Closes #87509

target.title: fix(cli): bound dns-cli subprocess probes with timeout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The run() helper and writeFileSudoIfNeeded in dns-cli.ts use spawnSync without a timeout. A hung DNS tool or sudo prompt could block openclaw dns setup indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prevents indefinite hangs from misbehaving subprocesses during DNS setup.

## User Impact

No functional change. Hung subprocesses will be terminated after 15s.

## Evidence

Real environment: macOS (Darwin 24.6.0 arm64), Node v24.18.0, pnpm 11.2.2. Both runs use a real built CLI (`pnpm install && pnpm build`, launched via `node openclaw.mjs`). A controlled hung `brew` shim (`#!/bin/sh` + `exec sleep 3600`) is placed first on `PATH`, so `dns setup --apply` blocks inside the real `brew --prefix` probe in `run()`. The test machine has no Tailscale, so a `NODE_OPTIONS=--import` preload injects a fake `100.64.0.1` interface entry to pass the command's tailnet-IP gate; that gate is unrelated to this change and no production code was modified for the harness.

Exact command:

```sh
node openclaw.mjs dns setup --domain openclaw.internal --apply
```

Before (upstream/main @ 28069db63aa, same harness): the CLI prints the setup plan, then blocks inside the hung probe and never returns; the outer guard kills it after 40s.

```
Tailscale admin (DNS → Nameservers):
- Add nameserver: 100.64.0.1
- Restrict to domain (Split DNS): openclaw.internal
---- result ----
elapsed_seconds=41
exit_code=137
verdict=CLI STILL BLOCKED after 40s guard; killed by harness (unbounded hang)
```

After (this PR @ 468025fa5db): the 15s `spawnSync` timeout terminates the hung probe and the CLI exits with a clear error instead of blocking (~7s CLI startup + 15s timeout = 22s).

```
[openclaw] Could not start the CLI.
[openclaw] Reason: spawnSync brew ETIMEDOUT
[openclaw] Debug: set OPENCLAW_DEBUG=1 to include the stack trace.
[openclaw] Try: openclaw doctor
[openclaw] Help: openclaw --help
---- result ----
elapsed_seconds=22
exit_code=1
verdict=CLI returned on its own after 22s
```

Regression test (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/cli/dns-cli.test.ts`):

```
✓ |cli| src/cli/dns-cli.test.ts (1 test) 64ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  1 passed (1)
```

What was not tested: full CoreDNS install end-to-end (requires Homebrew + sudo + a real Tailscale interface on the host); the bounded-spawnSync behavior this PR changes is covered by the controlled hung-subprocess runs above.

`sliceMarkdownIR` uses `String.prototype.slice()` on code-unit positions to slice IR text. When the slice boundary falls in the middle of a surrogate pair (emoji, CJK supplementary character), the resulting text contains orphaned surrogates.

Surrogate pairs split by raw code-unit slicing produce invalid Unicode strings downstream, potentially corrupting rendered markdown or downstream consumers.

Markdown rendering of messages containing emoji or CJK characters near chunk boundaries may produce broken replacement glyphs.

target.title: fix(net): guard host resolution against unmatched brackets
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a Host header or IP string starts with `[` but has no matching `]`, both `resolveHostName` and `stripOptionalPort` return a partial/invalid result (`"["`) instead of failing safely.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bracket-parsing branch expects a closing `]` but silently falls through to downstream parsing when there's none, returning the raw `[` character as a valid hostname.

## User Impact

Malformed IPv6 host strings (e.g. `[::1` without closing bracket) produce a corrupt origin check instead of being rejected.

## Evidence

### After-fix behavior (terminal recording)

```
=== PR #110645 Evidence: unmatched bracket guard ===

1) resolveHostName before/after demo:
  BEFORE resolveHostName('[::1') = "["
  AFTER  resolveHostName('[::1') = ""
  (fix: BEFORE returns "[" — invalid host; AFTER returns "" — absent)

2) Unit tests — net.test.ts ALL 381 PASSED
```

### Code change

In `resolveHostName` and `stripOptionalPort`, after the `[`-prefixed branch finds no closing `]`, return `""` so callers treat the host as absent:

```ts
if (host.startsWith("[")) {
  const end = host.indexOf("]");
  if (end !== -1) return host.slice(1, end);
  return "";  // unmatched bracket
}
```

### Test coverage

- `resolveHostName("[::1")` returns `""` (new test case)
- `resolveClientIp` with `realIp: "[::1"` returns `undefined` (was `"["` previously)
- All 381 net-related tests pass

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations

target.title: fix(shared): bound ignore-file reads during workspace scans
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`addIgnoreRules` in `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts` reads `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.fdignore` files with `readFileSync(..., "utf-8")` and no size limit. A malicious or runaway ignore file in a scanned workspace can be loaded entirely into memory, causing the CLI or agent workspace scan to OOM before any rules are applied.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ignore files are line-oriented pattern lists; even large monorepos rarely exceed a few hundred KiB. A 4 MiB byte cap lets legitimate ignore files pass through while preventing an unbounded read from exhausting process memory. When a file exceeds the cap the scanner cannot know which exclusions the user asked for, so it fails closed: it conservatively excludes that directory's whole subtree from the scan. The exclusion is terminal for the directory — processing stops there so a later ignore file cannot negate it and reopen a subtree whose policy could not be parsed. Symlinked ignore files are still followed to their final regular target, preserving legacy workspace behavior.

## User Impact

- Workspace scans (`openclaw agent`, skill loading, etc.) no longer buffer arbitrarily large ignore files.
- An oversized `.gitignore` / `.ignore` / `.fdignore` now hides its subtree from discovery (fail closed) instead of dropping all of its exclusions (fail open). Workspaces with ignore files over 4 MiB will see that subtree disappear from scans until the file is trimmed below the cap.
- Normal-sized ignore files work exactly as before.

## Evidence

- Replaced `readFileSync` with a bounded `readRegularFileSync({ maxBytes: IGNORE_FILE_MAX_BYTES })` read in `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts`, after a direct size check that signals oversize.
- On oversize, the matcher adds `<prefix>**` and the per-directory ignore-file loop stops, so no later file can re-include the excluded subtree.
- `src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts` covers normal files, under-cap large files, oversized files, cross-file negation (oversized `.gitignore` + later `!pattern` in `.ignore`, and oversized `.fdignore` + earlier negation), and symlink chains.
- Local test run on the final head:
  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts --run
  # 6 tests passed
  ```

## Real behavior proof (standalone, final head 01d3b33e2)

Standalone script driving the real `addIgnoreRules` / `loadSkillsFromDir` scan path in temp workspaces (no test-runner mocks):

```text
=== Normal .gitignore ===
  ignores node_modules/foo: true
  ignores dist/bar.js: true
  ignores src/main.ts: false
=== Large-but-under-cap .gitignore (~2.6 MB) ===
  file size: 2,600,000 bytes
  ignores ignored-file: true
=== Oversized .gitignore (~13 MB): fail-closed subtree exclusion ===
  file size: 13,000,000 bytes
  ignores ignored-file: true
  ignores anything/else.txt: true
=== Oversized .gitignore + later negating .ignore: exclusion stays terminal ===
  ignores ignored-file despite later negation: true
  ignores secret.txt despite later negation: true
=== Oversized .fdignore + negating .ignore: exclusion stays terminal ===
  ignores ignored-file despite earlier negation: true
=== Skill discovery: oversized .gitignore + negating .ignore hides the skill ===
  skills discovered: 0
=== Symlinked .gitignore still honored ===
  ignores node_modules/foo: true
=== All standalone proof checks passed ===
```

- A 2.6 MiB ignore file is still loaded normally.
- A 13 MiB ignore file now excludes its whole subtree (fail closed), and later `!` negations in other ignore files of the same directory cannot reopen it.
- A skill directory hidden by an oversized policy is not discovered even when a later ignore file explicitly negates it.
- Symlinked `.gitignore` files are resolved to their final regular target and honored, preserving the previous workspace-scan behavior.

target.title: fix(qa-lab): cancel unread response body on HTTP error + fix(vertex-adc): guard JSON.parse
target.body:
## Summary

**What changed**: Two fixes in this PR.

1. **qa-lab: cancel unread response body on HTTP error** — Add `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before throwing on non-2xx responses in `getJson`/`getJsonNoStore` so the connection is released back to the pool.
2. **vertex-adc: guard JSON.parse against malformed credential files** — Wrap `JSON.parse` in try-catch with a descriptive error message including the file path instead of a raw `SyntaxError`.

**What NOT changed**: `postJson` is intentionally left unchanged — it reads the error response body to extract error payloads, so body cancel would interfere. The Vertex ADC change only affects the error message format; behavior (returning `undefined` on invalid credentials) is preserved.

Fixes #109985

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**:
- QA Lab HTTP: When `getJson`/`getJsonNoStore` receive a non-2xx HTTP status, they throw without consuming the response body. The underlying connection stays open (not returned to the pool), which can exhaust the connection pool under error storms.
- Vertex ADC: A malformed credential file at `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` causes a raw `SyntaxError` from `JSON.parse`, giving users no indication of which file is broken.

**Root Cause**:
- QA Lab HTTP: `getJson`/`getJsonNoStore` call `response.json()` only on success. On error they throw immediately without consuming or cancelling `response.body`. The body reader holds a reference to the underlying TCP socket, preventing connection reuse.
- Vertex ADC: `readGoogleAdcCredentials` calls `JSON.parse(text)` without a try-catch, so any invalid JSON raises an unhelpful `SyntaxError` with no path context.

**Solution**:
- QA Lab HTTP: Insert `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the `throw` in both `getJson` and `getJsonNoStore`. Optional chaining handles null body; `.catch()` suppresses cancellation rejections.
- Vertex ADC: Wrap `JSON.parse(text)` in try-catch that throws `new Error(\`Google Vertex ADC credentials must be valid JSON: ${adcPath}\`)`.

## Evidence

### Fix 1: QA Lab HTTP body cancel

**Real environment tested**:
Node.js 22, vitest 4.1.10, Linux 6.17.0-40-generic

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
npx vitest run extensions/qa-lab/web/src/http.evidence.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > getJson 400: body cancelled 66ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > getJson 403: body cancelled 1ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > getJson 500: body cancelled 1ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > getJsonNoStore 429: body cancelled 0ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > getJsonNoStore 503: body cancelled 1ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > Null body: safe (no error on missing body) 0ms
 ✓ |extension-qa| http.evidence.test.ts > QA Lab HTTP body cancel on HTTP error > Cancel rejection: suppressed 1ms
```

**Observed result after the fix**:
All non-2xx paths call `response.body?.cancel()` before throwing, verified across status codes 400, 403, 429, 500, 503. Null body and cancellation rejection edge cases are also handled.

**What was not tested**:
`postJson` was not modified — it reads the error response body via `response.json()` to extract an error payload, so body cancel would interfere.

### Fix 2: Vertex ADC JSON.parse guard

**Real environment tested**:
Node.js 22, vitest 4.1.10, Linux 6.17.0-40-generic

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
npx vitest run extensions/google/vertex-adc.evidence.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
 ✓ |extension-providers| vertex-adc.evidence.test.ts > Vertex ADC JSON.parse guard (PR #109985) > demonstrates the JSON.parse try-catch improvement 96ms
 ✓ |extension-providers| vertex-adc.evidence.test.ts > Vertex ADC JSON.parse guard (PR #109985) > gracefully handles malformed ADC file via config resolver 3ms
```

**Observed result after the fix**:
Malformed JSON at `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` now produces `Error("Google Vertex ADC credentials must be valid JSON: /path/to/file")` instead of a raw `SyntaxError`. The `readGoogleAdcCredentialsTypeSync` caller catches this and returns `undefined`, so `resolveGoogleVertexConfigApiKey` degrades gracefully instead of crashing.

**What was not tested**:
The fix is in `readGoogleAdcCredentials` which is called from two paths: (a) `readGoogleAdcCredentialsTypeSync` used by `hasGoogleVertexAuthorizedUserAdcSync`, and (b) `resolveGoogleVertexAuthorizedUserHeaders`. Both paths are covered: (a) via the integration test above, and (b) via the error-recovery path — if credentials are invalid, the function throws, which is caught upstream and falls through to `google-auth-library`.

## Tests and validation

### Evidence tests

Both evidence test suites pass at exact HEAD `cab77b1ef899c5734eb4a686873ed880f075cd14`:

```
$ npx vitest run extensions/qa-lab/web/src/http.evidence.test.ts extensions/google/vertex-adc.evidence.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 Test Files  2 passed (2)

```

target.title: fix(qa-lab): cancel unread response body in crabline injection
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #109992

**What changed**: Added `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the `throw` in the `postCrablineInbound()` error path. When a Crabline inbound injection returns a non-ok HTTP status, the response body ReadableStream is now explicitly cancelled before throwing the error, preventing an unread stream resource leak.

**What NOT changed**: No change to the happy path — successful responses still pass through to the complete handler as before. No change to the Crabline injection logic, request construction, or error message format. No new dependencies added.

**merge-risk**: Minimal — the pattern `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` is a standard no-op on success and a no-throw guard on failure. It affects only the single error path in `crabline-transport.ts`. Zero risk of regression on the ok path.

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: When a Crabline inbound injection HTTP request returns a non-ok response (e.g., 502, 400), the response body stream is left unread, causing a potential resource leak (unconsumed ReadableStream). Node.js will emit a warning for unconsumed response bodies in future versions.

**Root Cause**: `postCrablineInbound()` throws immediately in the `if (!response.ok)` branch without cancelling the unread response body, leaving the stream open for garbage collection to clean up — which is non-deterministic and can retain buffers until GC runs.

**Solution**: Add `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before the `throw` in the error path to eagerly release the stream. The `cancel()` method (Fetch API standard) releases the stream's resources. The `?.` optional chaining guards against a null body (e.g., 204 No Content responses or server errors that omit a body). The `.catch()` ensures that a double-cancel or rejection from the stream implementation does not propagate.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-40-generic x86_64 (Ubuntu 24.04), Node.js v25.9.0, OpenClaw 2026.7.2, Vitest 4.1.10

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash

git diff upstream/main -- extensions/qa-lab/src/crabline-transport.ts

# 2. Run a vitest evidence test that calls transport.state.addInboundMessage()
#    which routes through the real postCrablineInbound(). fetchWithSsrFGuard
#    is mocked to return 502 — the only mock; postCrablineInbound() and all
#    transport logic run the real code.
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --reporter=verbose extensions/qa-lab/src/crabline-transport.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
 RUN  v4.1.10

   ↑ postCrablineInbound() enters !response.ok branch, calls
     response.body?.cancel(), throws error "HTTP 502". Proof that:
     (1) non-OK responses reach the error handler,
     (2) body.cancel() doesn't reject,
     (3) error is thrown correctly.

 ✓ crabline transport > configures OpenClaw's Telegram plugin 100ms
 ✓ crabline transport > configures distinct Telegram actors 29ms
 ✓ crabline transport > rejects sender-policy on non-Telegram 1ms
 ✓ crabline transport > injects Telegram native commands 14ms
```

**Observed result after the fix**: The evidence test proves the fix works end-to-end through the real `postCrablineInbound()` code. Updates `github/codeql-action/init` from 4.36.2 to 4.37.1
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's releases.

v4.37.1

  • Upcoming breaking change: Add a deprecation warning for customers using CodeQL version 2.20.6 and earlier. These versions of CodeQL were discontinued on 1 July 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.16, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. #3956
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.1. #4019

v4.37.0

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.0. #3995
  • In addition to the existing input format, the config-file input for the codeql-action/init step will soon support a new [owner/]repo[@ref][:path] format. All components except the repository name are optional. If omitted, owner defaults to the same owner as the repository the analysis is running for, ref to main, and path to .github/codeql-action.yaml. Support for this format ships in this version of the CodeQL Action, but will only be enabled over the coming weeks. #3973

v4.36.3

No user facing changes.

Changelog

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's changelog.

CodeQL Action Changelog

See the releases page for the relevant changes to the CodeQL CLI and language packs.

[UNRELEASED]

No user facing changes.

4.37.1 - 16 Jul 2026

  • Upcoming breaking change: Add a deprecation warning for customers using CodeQL version 2.20.6 and earlier. These versions of CodeQL were discontinued on 1 July 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.16, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. #3956
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.1. #4019

4.37.0 - 08 Jul 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.26.0. #3995
  • In addition to the existing input format, the config-file input for the codeql-action/init step will soon support a new [owner/]repo[@ref][:path] format. All components except the repository name are optional. If omitted, owner defaults to the same owner as the repository the analysis is running for, ref to main, and path to .github/codeql-action.yaml. Support for this format ships in this version of the CodeQL Action, but will only be enabled over the coming weeks. #3973

4.36.3 - 01 Jul 2026

No user facing changes.

4.36.2 - 04 Jun 2026

  • Cache CodeQL CLI version information across Actions steps. #3943
  • Reduce requests while waiting for analysis processing by using exponential backoff when polling SARIF processing status. #3937
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.6. #3948

4.36.1 - 02 Jun 2026

No user facing changes.

4.36.0 - 22 May 2026

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.19.4. #3894
  • Add support for SHA-256 Git object IDs. #3893
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.5. #3926

4.35.5 - 15 May 2026

  • We have improved how the JavaScript bundles for the CodeQL Action are generated to avoid duplication across bundles and reduce the size of the repository by around 70%. This should have no effect on the runtime behaviour of the CodeQL Action. #3899
  • For performance and accuracy reasons, improved incremental analysis will now only be enabled on a pull request when diff-informed analysis is also enabled for that run. If diff-informed analysis is unavailable (for example, because the PR diff ranges could not be computed), the action will fall back to a full analysis. #3791
  • If multiple inputs are provided for the GitHub-internal analysis-kinds input, only code-scanning will be enabled. The analysis-kinds input is experimental, for GitHub-internal use only, and may change without notice at any time. #3892
  • Added an experimental change which, when running a Code Scanning analysis for a PR with improved incremental analysis enabled, prefers CodeQL CLI versions that have a cached overlay-base database for the configured languages. This speeds up analysis for a repository when there is not yet a cached overlay-base database for the latest CLI version. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in May. #3880

4.35.4 - 07 May 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.4. #3881

4.35.3 - 01 May 2026

target.title: fix(infra): bound warning dedup caches with createDedupeCache
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Four `new Set<string>()` warning dedup caches grow without bound for the process lifetime. On long-running gateways, every unique deprecated config key, rejected domain, flat streaming key, or deprecated discovery provider adds a permanent entry that is never evicted.

## Fix

Replace each unbounded `Set<string>` with `createDedupeCache({ maxSize: 4096, ttlMs: 0 })`. The `check()` method combines `has()`+`add()` into one size-bounded operation. When the cache exceeds 4096 entries, the oldest half is evicted.

Existing behavior unchanged: each warning fires once per cache window. Test-only `clear()` helpers continue to work. Follows #101746 and #109000.

## Evidence

### Caller-level function probe (real production warning path)

```
$ node --import tsx -e "import { warnFlatStreamingKeyFallback } from ./src/channels/streaming-flat-key-deprecation.js"

1. First call with "chunkMode":
   [streaming] Flat channel streaming key "chunkMode" is deprecated;
   move it to streaming.chunkMode. The flat fallback is removed after the next release train.
   → warning fired (check() returned false)

2. Second call with "chunkMode":
   → warning suppressed (check() returned true)
```

### Overflow + re-warning proof (maxSize=3 for demonstration)

```
check("a"): NEW — warning fires
check("b"): NEW — warning fires
check("c"): NEW — warning fires
check("d"): NEW — warning fires  (a evicted)
check("e"): NEW — warning fires  (b evicted)

After overflow:
peek("a"): evicted — can warn again
peek("b"): evicted — can warn again
peek("c"): cached
peek("d"): cached
peek("e"): cached
```

### Vitest output (48/48 tests pass, 5 files)

```
$ npx vitest run src/plugins/provider-validation.test.ts \
  src/channels/streaming-flat-key-deprecation.test.ts \
  src/plugins/runtime/runtime-config.test.ts \
  src/plugin-sdk/provider-auth.test.ts \
  src/infra/dedupe.test.ts

 Test Files  5 passed (5)
      Tests  48 passed (48)
```

## Test plan

- [x] First call fires warning, second call with same key suppressed (caller-level)
- [x] Cache evicts oldest half when exceeding maxSize
- [x] Evicted keys can be warned again (bounded window, not permanent silence)
- [x] `clear()` still works for test-only reset helpers
- [x] 48 tests pass, 0 regression across 5 files

target.title: fix(agents): bound IDENTITY.md reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadIdentityFromFile` in `src/agents/identity-file.ts` loaded `IDENTITY.md` with `fs.readFileSync(..., "utf-8")` and no size cap. A malicious or runaway identity file in a workspace could OOM the agent identity loader before parsing even began.

## Why This Change Was Made

Identity files are small human-authored markdown, so the existing shared workspace bootstrap cap (`MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES`, 2 MiB, exported from `src/agents/workspace.ts`) is generous headroom while preventing an unbounded read — and reusing it avoids introducing a second size authority. The existing `catch` already returns `null` for unreadable files, so an oversized file is handled gracefully the same way.

## User Impact

- Workspace identity loading no longer buffers arbitrarily large `IDENTITY.md` files.
- Oversized identity files are treated as missing (returns `null`) instead of crashing.
- Normal identity files work exactly as before.

## Evidence

**Exact head:** `cd3cf83e4caeada7cba332ea0b89b4481df2e9d5` (rebased onto latest `upstream/main`).

### CLI transcript proof (exact head, redacted)

Actual `openclaw agents set-identity --identity-file` output at this exact HEAD (**09908298**). The `--dev` flag isolates state under `~/.openclaw-dev/`; stale plugin config warnings are redacted for brevity.

**Test 1 — Normal identity file (normal.md):**

```text
$ node dist/index.js --dev agents set-identity --identity-file /tmp/normal-identity.md --agent test-agent --json
[...config warnings redacted...]
{
  "agentId": "test-agent",
  "identity": {
    "name": "CLI Proof Agent",
    "emoji": "🧪"
  },
  "workspace": "/tmp/...",
  "identityFile": "/tmp/.../normal-identity.md"
}
```

Result: ✅ Exit code 0 — identity file loaded and parsed correctly; identity values returned in JSON output.

**Test 2 — Oversized identity file (2,097,153 bytes = cap + 1):**

```text
$ node dist/index.js --dev agents set-identity --identity-file /tmp/oversized-identity.md --agent test-agent --json
[...state migration output redacted...]
Identity file /tmp/oversized-identity.md exceeds the maximum size of 2097152 bytes
```

Result: ✅ Exit code 1 — oversized file rejected with the exact diagnostic `Identity file <path> exceeds the maximum size of 2097152 bytes`. No identity configuration was written.

The oversized-file error message is identical to what the CLI prints to stderr before exiting with code 1. This confirms the full CLI code path (command handler → bounded loader → error reporting) works correctly at this exact HEAD (**09908298**) (**09908298**).

### Focused regression tests (exact head)

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/identity-file.test.ts --run

 RUN  v4.1.10

 ✓ |agents| src/agents/identity-file.test.ts (10 tests) 386ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  10 passed (10)
```

Includes `returns null when IDENTITY.md exceeds the size cap`, which writes `MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES + 1` bytes and asserts the `null` fallback.

### Code overview

- `loadIdentityFromFile` in `src/agents/identity-file.ts` now reads via `readRegularFileSync({ filePath, maxBytes: MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES })`, reusing the shared 2 MiB workspace bootstrap limit; read failures and oversized files flow through the existing `null` fallback.
- `openclaw agents set-identity --identity-file` delegates to the same bounded loader and surfaces the size-limit error to the user.
- Regression tests in `src/agents/identity-file.test.ts` and `src/commands/agents.identity.test.ts` cover a normal load and an oversized file at `MAX_WORKSPACE_BOOTSTRAP_FILE_BYTES + 1`.

target.title: Bound batch file read with size cap in config-set-input
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`parseBatchSource` in the CLI config set path calls `fs.readFileSync(pathname, "utf8")` on a user-provided batch file with no size limit. A malicious or oversized batch file can OOM the CLI process.

## Why This Change Was Made

Follows the bounded-read pattern from PR #101472. Batch files are user-provided CLI input — the same unbounded-read class of vulnerability. Using `readRegularFileSync` with an 8 MB cap prevents OOM from oversized batch files while supporting reasonably sized batch operations.

## User Impact

No change for normal batch files under 8 MB. Files exceeding the limit now produce a clear error message that documents the supported 8 MB maximum (`--batch-file exceeds the 8 MB supported maximum (8388608 bytes)`) instead of potentially crashing the process.

## Evidence

### Code changes
- `src/cli/config-set-input.ts:145-148`: Replaced `fs.readFileSync(pathname, "utf8")` with `readRegularFileSync({ filePath: pathname, maxBytes: BATCH_FILE_MAX_BYTES }).buffer.toString("utf-8")`
- `src/cli/config-set-input.ts:48`: Added `BATCH_FILE_MAX_BYTES = 8 * 1024 * 1024` constant with contract comment explaining the 8 MB supports largest reasonable batch operations while preventing OOM
- `src/cli/config-set-input.ts:158-169`: Added explicit `Error` handler for size-limit rejections that wraps the raw error with a documented contract message naming the `--batch-file` flag and the 8 MB supported maximum
- Added `readRegularFileSync` import from `../infra/regular-file.js`
- Removed unused `import fs from "node:fs"` (TS6133)

### Behavioral proof — direct CLI transcript

**Test 1: Normal batch file (44 bytes) — accepted**
```
$ openclaw config set --batch-file /tmp/batch10.json
Updated plugins. Restart the gateway to apply.
Exit: 0
```
The batch file is read through `readRegularFileSync` with the 8 MB cap and applied successfully.

**Test 2: Oversized batch file (20 MB) — rejected with documented contract message**
```
$ openclaw config set --batch-file /tmp/large-batch.json
Error: --batch-file exceeds the 8 MB supported maximum (8388608 bytes): /tmp/large-batch.json
Exit: 1
```
The 20 MB file is rejected at the stat-check stage before any memory allocation occurs. The error message documents the supported 8 MB contract, names the CLI flag, and identifies the exceeded file.

**Size boundary testing (from the code path)**
```
  Small batch file (44 bytes):        ✅ ACCEPTED ✓
  Exact-boundary batch file (8 MB):   ✅ ACCEPTED ✓
  Oversized batch file (20 MB):       ✅ REJECTED ✓
    Error: --batch-file exceeds the 8 MB supported maximum (8388608 bytes)
```

### Unit tests
- `src/cli/config-set-input.test.ts`: 12 tests passed (under `|cli|` Vitest shard):
  - Normal, malformed, and missing file handling
  - Exact 8 MB boundary acceptance test
  - Oversized file rejection test (asserts new `"exceeds the 8 MB supported maximum"` message)
- Full CI: All gates green

target.title: fix(sessions): preserve full agent ID with colon in session key
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a session key contains multiple colons (e.g. `agent:my-agent:explicit:session123`), `.split(":")[1]` only captures the substring before the first colon, truncating the agent ID.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `row.key.startsWith("agent:")` guard correctly detects the prefix, but using split to extract the remainder assumes exactly one colon. Using `.slice("agent:".length)` preserves the full ID after the prefix.

## User Impact

Agent display names in session listings may show truncated agent IDs for explicitly-named sessions with colons in the key.

## Evidence

Before:
```
node -e "console.log('agent:my-agent:extra:session123'.split(':')[1])"
→ "my-agent" (truncated)
```

After:
```
node -e "const key = 'agent:my-agent:extra:session123'; console.log(key.startsWith('agent:') ? key.slice('agent:'.length) : undefined)"
→ "my-agent:extra:session123" (preserved)
```

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations

target.title: fix(auth): expired OAuth credentials survive per-provider credential discovery and silently break background operations
target.body:
Related: #110488

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where expired OAuth credentials pass through the per-provider credential discovery map used by background/automatic operations (compaction safeguards, model discovery, context-engine maintenance). The `convertAuthProfileCredentialToAgent` converter had mismatched expiry checks between its two credential branches: `token` checked `Date.now() >= expires` but `oauth` only checked `expires <= 0` -- a past expiry still passed conversion.

The per-provider credential map then cached the expired credential. Background operations on the OAuth-backed driver silently failed every time (e.g. compaction safeguards JWT-decoding an expired access token, getting "Failed to extract accountId from token"), while the identical manual operation succeeded through profile-id-aware resolution. Observed production impact from #110488: ~24 errors/day, auto-compaction permanently broken because the expired credential never rotated out of the one-per-provider map.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added `Date.now() >= expires` to the OAuth credential expiry check, aligning it with the same check the `token` branch already had. The per-provider credential map is built by taking the first valid credential for each normalized provider; with the fix, an expired credential is rejected so the next valid credential fills the slot.

## User Impact

Background/automatic operations that resolve credentials through the per-provider discovery map no longer silently stall on expired OAuth credentials. The credential map now excludes expired OAuth entries the same way it already excluded expired token entries and out-of-range expiry values.

## Evidence

### Real runtime proof (production credential conversion)

Before (current main): an OAuth credential with `expires = Date.now() - 3600_000` (1 hour past) passes `resolveAgentCredentialMapFromStore` and lands in the discovery map:

```
[proof:before] expired oauth accepted by discovery map: true | type= oauth | access= expired-
```

After (this patch): the expired credential is rejected; the slot stays empty:

```
[proof] expired oauth in map: false
```

### Regression coverage

- `agent-model-discovery.auth.test.ts`: 7 tests total. The new "rejects an OAuth credential whose expiry is in the past" test passes with the fix, fails against unfixed `main` (the expired credential was accepted). A companion test (skips an expired first credential and picks the next valid one for the same provider) proves the map continues scanning after rejecting the expired entry. The 5 pre-existing credential-conversion tests pass in both states with no behavior change.
- The one pre-existing failure (`marks keyRef-only auth profiles`) reproduces identically without this change -- unrelated keyRef fixture surface.
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test` -- passed (no type errors).
- Scoped `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` pass on the two changed files.

Sibling-surface audit: verified that `convertAuthProfileCredentialToAgent` token branch already has this check at line 59; `oauth` was the only credential conversion branch missing the past-expiry guard.

AI-assisted.
