target.title: fix(codex): reject hex/exponent computer wait duration strings
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Codex computer `wait` / `hold_key` outer watchdog deadlines used JavaScript `Number(...)` on free-form `duration` values. Hex strings such as `"0x10"` were accepted (`Number("0x10") === 16`) and silently inflated the deadline, while the downstream computer tool already rejects hex via `readFiniteNumberParam` → `parseStrictFiniteNumber`.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Codex contract (sibling `../codex` inspected):** dynamic-tool arguments are `serde_json::Value` with no field-level `duration` guard — `DynamicToolHandler` parses JSON and forwards the value unchanged (`codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/dynamic.rs:136`, checkout `bdd282f3bbd55df3a869a5438519cd948c134d4d`). OpenClaw pins `@openai/codex@0.144.4`.

**Canonical downstream grammar (OpenClaw computer tool):**
- Schema: `optionalFiniteNumberSchema` in `src/agents/tools/computer-tool.ts:161`
- Runtime: `readFiniteNumberParam` → `readNumberParam({ strict: true })` → `parseStrictFiniteNumber` (`src/agents/tools/common.ts:228`, `computer-tool.ts:856`)

That parser **rejects hex** (`"0x10"`) and **accepts** decimal / scientific / fractional strings (`"100"`, `"1e2"`, `"100.5"`, `"0.5"`) plus finite numbers.

This PR makes the Codex outer watchdog use the **same** `parseStrictFiniteNumber` path so hex inflation is fixed without underbudgeting fractional/scientific strings that computer-tool still honors.

Collision: overlaps [#107623](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/107623); this head is the rebased, contract-aligned form.

## User Impact

| Duration input | Before (`Number()`) | After (computer-tool grammar) |
|---|---|---|
| `"0x10"` | +16s inflation | baseline (rejected) |
| `"1e2"` / `"100.5"` / `"0.5"` | coerced | honored (aligned) |
| `0.5` (number) | honored | honored |

## Evidence

Exact head: `d85b72dabe57770b68e901f974a448729cf05581`

### Call path

```
Codex app-server request
  → run-attempt-server-requests.ts:191  resolveDynamicToolCallTimeoutMs({ call, config })
    → dynamic-tool-execution.ts:499     readComputerToolTimeoutMs(value)
      → dynamic-tool-execution.ts:517   readComputerDurationMs(args.duration)
        → parseStrictFiniteNumber(value)   ← same grammar as computer-tool
```

The changed function `resolveDynamicToolCallTimeoutMs` is **the exact entry point** called from the real Codex app-server dynamic-tool request handler at `run-attempt-server-requests.ts:191`. No additional transformation or argument rewriting occurs between the Codex request and the timeout resolution.

### Format and diff check

```
$ git diff --check origin/main..HEAD && echo ok
ok
```

### Vitest suite — 30 tests covering all duration edge cases

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-execution.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  30 passed (30)
```

The new test `"aligns computer duration strings with computer-tool parseStrictFiniteNumber"` exercises `resolveDynamicToolCallTimeoutMs` with real `computer` tool-call payloads — the exact call shape from `run-attempt-server-requests.ts:191`. It verifies:

| Input | Expected timeout | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `"0x10"` (hex) | 120_000ms | Rejected → baseline |
| `"1e2"` (scientific) | 250_000ms | Honored (100s) |
| `"100.5"` (fraction) | 220_500ms | Honored (100.5s) |
| `"0.5"` (fraction) | 120_500ms | Honored (0.5s) |
| `0.5` (numeric) | 120_500ms | Honored |
| `"100"` (decimal) | 220_000ms | Honored |

All 30 existing tests continue to pass — no regression.

### Mutation check

Revert `readComputerDurationMs` → `Number()`:
```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-execution.test.ts -t "aligns computer"

 FAIL  ... > aligns computer duration strings with computer-tool parseStrictFiniteNumber
AssertionError: expected 136000 to be 120000
    at extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-execution.test.ts:251:12

 Tests  1 failed | 29 skipped (30)
```

`Number("0x10")` = 16 inflates the deadline to 136000ms instead of the expected 120000ms baseline. Restore `readComputerDurationMs` → 30/30 passed.

### Grammar alignment verification

`parseStrictFiniteNumber` — the same function shared by both the Codex watchdog and the downstream computer tool:

```
parseStrictFiniteNumber("0x10")   → undefined  (hex rejected ✓)
parseStrictFiniteNumber("100")    → 100        (decimal honored ✓)
parseStrictFiniteNumber("1e2")    → 100        (scientific honored ✓)
parseStrictFiniteNumber("100.5")  → 100.5      (fraction honored ✓)
parseStrictFiniteNumber(100)      → 100        (numeric honored ✓)
parseStrictFiniteNumber("abc")    → undefined  (garbage rejected ✓)
```

### Codex dependency contract

- `../codex/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/dynamic.rs:127-142` — no field-level `duration` guard; `serde_json::Value` forwarded unchanged to OpenClaw
- `@openai/codex@0.144.4` — pinned version
- OpenClaw receives the raw JSON duration value and now parses it with the same grammar as the downstream computer tool

### Not tested

- Live Codex app-server roundtrip with real API key (the test exercises the exact same `resolveDynamicToolCallTimeoutMs` entry point and call shape as the live path at `run-attempt-server-requests.ts:191`)
- Non-computer dynamic tool timeout paths: unchanged — all 29 existing non-computer tests pass

target.title: Bound diagnostic config file read with size cap
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readConfigExport` in the diagnostic support export path calls `fs.readFileSync(options.configPath, "utf8")` on the user's config file with no size limit. A corrupted or enormous config file can OOM the diagnostic export path, preventing support bundle generation.

## Why This Change Was Made

PR #101472 established the bounded-read pattern. The diagnostic export path reads the user's config file to include sanitized config in support bundles. Config files are user-controlled content and should not be trusted to have reasonable size. Using `readRegularFileSync` with an 8 MB cap (config files are typically <100 KB) prevents OOM from corrupted config files while maintaining diagnostic value.

## User Impact

No user-visible change under normal conditions. Config files under 8 MB export identically to before. An oversized config file results in a graceful config-shape-read-failure entry in the diagnostic report instead of crashing the export.

## Evidence

### Code changes
- `src/logging/diagnostic-support-export.ts:348-350`: Replaced `fs.readFileSync(options.configPath, "utf8")` with `readRegularFileSync({ filePath: options.configPath, maxBytes: DIAGNOSTIC_CONFIG_MAX_BYTES }).buffer.toString("utf8")`
- `src/logging/diagnostic-support-export.ts:41`: Added `DIAGNOSTIC_CONFIG_MAX_BYTES = 8 * 1024 * 1024` constant
- Added `readRegularFileSync` import from `../infra/regular-file.js`
- Existing error handling already catches and reports read failures gracefully

### Behavioral proof — real diagnostic export (via `writeDiagnosticSupportExport`)

Both scenarios call the actual `writeDiagnosticSupportExport` function with real temp directories, real config files, and real zip output validated by decompression and content inspection.

**Test 1: Normal config file (~100 bytes) — accepted, parseOk: true**
```
Config file: {"gateway":{"mode":"local","port":18789},"logging":{"redactSensitive":"off"}}
Config file size: 78 bytes
Export generated: /tmp/.../support-normal.zip
config/shape.json parseOk: true
Config values present: gateway.mode=local, gateway.port=18789
Result: ✅ PASS
```

The config is read through `readRegularFileSync` with the 8 MB cap, parsed as JSON5, and included in the support bundle with `parseOk: true` and all config values correctly present.

**Test 2: Oversized config file (8 MB + 1 byte) — rejected, parseOk: false, bundle still complete**
```
Config file size: 8388609 bytes (exceeds 8 MB cap)
Export generated: /tmp/.../support-oversized.zip
config/shape.json parseOk: false
Error in shape: "File exceeds 8388608 bytes: ..."
Bundle still has diagnostics.json: true
Bundle still has manifest.json: true
Bundle has support footer: true
Result: ✅ PASS
```

The oversized file is rejected at the stat-check stage by `readRegularFileSync` with `File exceeds 8388608 bytes`. The bundle still contains `diagnostics.json`, `manifest.json`, and the standard support footer.

### Unit tests
- `src/logging/diagnostic-support-export.test.ts`:
  - `✓ reads a normal-size config file and reports parseOk: true` (752ms)
  - `✓ handles an oversized config file exceeding the 8 MB read cap gracefully` (30ms)
- Total: 2/2 new tests passed, 13/13 total in file
- Full CI: All gates green

### Proof command
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs "src/logging/diagnostic-support-export.test.ts" -t "reads a normal-size config|handles an oversized config"
```

## Related
- PR #101472 (established `readRegularFileSync` bounded-read pattern in `src/cron/store.ts`)
- PR #110592 (bounded doctor-workspace reads with read-before-archive ordering)
- PR #110593 (bounded config-set-input batch-file reads)
- PR #110594 (bounded bundle-command file reads with oversized diagnostic)

target.title: fix(sqlite): normalize BLOB/TEXT type mismatches during STRICT migration
target.body:
Related to #110186

## What Problem This Solves

The STRICT migration introduced in v2026.7.2 crashes the gateway on startup when legacy non-STRICT SQLite tables contain BLOB values in TEXT columns (or TEXT values in BLOB columns). The `INSERT INTO strict SELECT * FROM legacy` statement rejects the type mismatch, aborts the entire migration transaction, and leaves the gateway in a crash-loop with no in-product recovery — users must manually edit their SQLite database to proceed.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `node:sqlite` driver writes `Buffer.from()` JavaScript values as SQLite BLOB type. In non-STRICT tables, these BLOB values silently coexist in TEXT columns. When PR #108663 introduced STRICT migration, it used a bare `INSERT INTO strict SELECT col1, col2 FROM legacy` that passes values through without type normalization. STRICT tables enforce column types, so BLOB-in-TEXT (or TEXT-in-BLOB) rows abort the INSERT and roll back the entire transaction.

Non-STRICT SQLite also allows BLOB and TEXT values with the same byte content to coexist as separate rows under a TEXT PRIMARY KEY (they have different stored types, so the UNIQUE constraint sees them as distinct). After CAST, these would collide. The migration detects this collision and fails with an actionable error rather than silently discarding data, consistent with the project's fail-closed policy for ambiguous persisted-state decisions.

Note: the linked issue #110186 also describes rowid-model and stale-lease startup failures that this PR does not change; those symptoms need separate resolution.

## User Impact

- Users upgrading from v2026.7.1 to v2026.7.2 whose databases contain BLOB values in TEXT columns (e.g., `config_health_entries.last_known_good_json`) no longer crash-loop
- The STRICT migration normalizes BLOB→TEXT and TEXT→BLOB via `CAST`, preserving all row data instead of aborting
- If BLOB and TEXT primary key values would collide after CAST, the migration fails with a clear error message directing the user to `openclaw doctor --fix` or manual cleanup — no data is silently discarded
- `openclaw doctor --fix` and the normal startup migration path both benefit — same fix, same code path

## Scope Boundary: Secondary UNIQUE Constraints

This PR preflights normalized collisions for **PRIMARY KEY** columns only. Secondary UNIQUE constraints (table-level `UNIQUE`, `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX`) are **not** preflighted:

- OpenClaw production code never writes `Buffer.from()` values to secondary UNIQUE TEXT columns (`event_id`, `source_id`, `dedupe_key`, `subscription_id`, `credential_hash`, `provision_operation_id`, etc.). The only confirmed BLOB-in-TEXT production case is `config_health_entries.last_known_good_json`, whose table has no secondary UNIQUE constraints.
- If a secondary UNIQUE constraint did collide after CAST, the migration would fail with a generic SQLite `UNIQUE constraint failed` error rather than a targeted diagnosis. This is an accepted scope limitation.
- Maintaining collision preflight for every UNIQUE index (including partial indexes with `WHERE` clauses) would add disproportionate complexity for a theoretical risk that has zero observed production instances.

Maintainers have reviewed and accepted this scope decision. If secondary UNIQUE collisions are ever observed in production, the preflight can be extended in a follow-up.

## Evidence

**Real environment**: Linux, Node v24.18.0 (SQLite bundled), current head of `fix/strict-blob-text-cast-110186`

### Real v2026.7.1→current upgrade through repairOpenClawStateDatabaseSchema

Created a canonical state database, downgraded `config_health_entries` to non-STRICT (simulating v2026.7.1), inserted a BLOB-in-TEXT row via `Buffer.from('{"api_key":"sk-prod-redacted"}')`, then ran `repairOpenClawStateDatabaseSchema`:

```
=== Pre-downgrade (STRICT) ===
  path=/home/user/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.json vtype=null
  path=/home/user/.openclaw/openclaw.json vtype=text

BLOB row: {"config_path":"/home/user/.openclaw/credentials/ai.json","vtype":"blob"}

=== Running repairOpenClawStateDatabaseSchema (doctor) ===
Result: {
  "changes": [
    "Migrated shared state session watch cursors → provenance column (0 ambient, 0 sentinels removed)",
    "Migrated shared state tables to SQLite STRICT typing (1)"
  ],
  "warnings": []
}

STRICT flag: {"strict":1}

Post-migration rows:
  path=/home/user/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.json type=null value=null
  path=/home/user/.openclaw/credentials/ai.json type=text value={"api_key":"sk-prod-redacted"}
  path=/home/user/.openclaw/openclaw.json type=text value={"defaultModel":"sonnet-4.6"}
```

The BLOB value was correctly normalized to TEXT. All three rows migrated successfully with correct types and values. The doctor path completed without warnings.

### Scenario Matrix

| Source type | Canonical column type | CAST behavior | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| BLOB (Buffer) in TEXT column | TEXT | `CAST(col AS TEXT)` | ✅ typeof=TEXT, value preserved as UTF-8 string |
| TEXT string in BLOB column | BLOB | `CAST(col AS BLOB)` | ✅ typeof=BLOB, bytes preserved |
| TEXT in TEXT column (normal) | TEXT | `CAST(col AS TEXT)` | ✅ Idempotent, no change |
| BLOB in BLOB column (normal) | BLOB | `CAST(col AS BLOB)` | ✅ Idempotent, no change |
| NULL in TEXT column | TEXT | `CAST(col AS TEXT)` | ✅ NULL unchanged |
| INTEGER in TEXT column | TEXT | No CAST needed | ✅ STRICT auto-coerces INTEGER→TEXT |
| Non-UTF-8 BLOB in TEXT column | TEXT | `CAST(col AS TEXT)` | ✅ Bytes preserved, typeof=TEXT (SQLite does not validate UTF-8) |
| BLOB PK collides with TEXT PK after CAST | TEXT | Fail-safe error | ✅ Migration rejected with actionable error; no data silently discarded |
| BLOB PK with no TEXT collision | TEXT | `CAST(pk AS TEXT)` | ✅ Row preserved, PK value converted to TEXT |

### Test output (engine-level, 20 tests)

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/sqlite-strict.test.ts --run
 ✓ |infra| src/infra/sqlite-strict.test.ts (20 tests) 176ms
     ✓ normalizes BLOB values in TEXT columns during STRICT migration
     ✓ normalizes TEXT values in BLOB columns during STRICT migration
     ✓ normalizes mixed-type rows in TEXT columns without losing values
     ✓ rejects STRICT migration when BLOB and TEXT primary key rows collide after CAST
     ✓ preserves BLOB primary key rows when no TEXT collision exists
     ✓ normalizes non-UTF-8 BLOB bytes in TEXT columns during STRICT migration
     ✓ allows composite-key rows when BLOB component matches but full tuple is unique
     ✓ rejects composite-key rows when full tuple collides after CAST
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  20 passed (20)
```

### Test output (state-DB doctor upgrade, 85 tests)

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/state/openclaw-state-db.test.ts --run
 ✓ |unit| src/state/openclaw-state-db.test.ts (85 tests)
     ✓ doctor migrates legacy BLOB values in TEXT columns to STRICT without losing rows
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  85 passed (85)
```

### Test output (agent-DB upgrade, 45 tests)

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/state/openclaw-agent-db.test.ts --run
 ✓ |unit| src/state/openclaw-agent-db.test.ts (45 tests)
     ✓ migrates legacy BLOB values in TEXT columns to STRICT without losing agent state
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  45 passed (45)
```

### Codex Review Resolution

| Requirement | Status | Implementation |
|---|---|---|
| Real v2026.7.1→current upgrade proof via doctor/gateway | ✅ Addressed | Full `repairOpenClawStateDatabaseSchema` run with BLOB data shown above |
| BLOB-to-TEXT normalization collision coverage | ✅ Addressed | Test: `rejects STRICT migration when BLOB and TEXT primary key rows collide after CAST` — migration fails with actionable error |
| Composite primary key collision coverage | ✅ Addressed | Tests: `allows composite-key rows when BLOB component matches but full tuple is unique` + `rejects composite-key rows when full tuple collides after CAST` |
| Non-text BLOB byte handling | ✅ Addressed | Test: `normalizes non-UTF-8 BLOB bytes in TEXT columns during STRICT migration` — bytes preserved, typeof=TEXT |
| Secondary UNIQUE constraint collisions | ✅ Scope accepted | Documented in "Scope Boundary" section above; production code never writes BLOB to these columns |
| Fail-safe for ambiguous conversion | ✅ Addressed | PK collision detection uses EXISTS subquery — colliding rows cause clear error directing user to `openclaw doctor --fix` |
| Closing link scope | ✅ Addressed | Changed `Closes #110186` to `Related to #110186` — issue also covers rowid-model and stale-lease failures |

## What Changed

**`src/infra/sqlite-strict.ts`** (+76/-6):

- Added `columnTypes: Map<string, string>` and `primaryKeyColumns: string[]` to `CanonicalStrictTable`
- `readCanonicalStrictTables` now collects column types and PK columns via `PRAGMA table_xinfo`
- Before the INSERT, for tables with TEXT primary key columns, the migration detects BLOB/TEXT PK collisions and fails with an actionable error rather than silently discarding data
- The INSERT statement now uses `CAST(col AS TEXT)` for TEXT columns and `CAST(col AS BLOB)` for BLOB columns; all other columns (INTEGER, REAL, rowid alias) are passed through unchanged

**`src/infra/sqlite-strict.test.ts`** (+134):

- `normalizes BLOB values in TEXT columns during STRICT migration`
- `normalizes TEXT values in BLOB columns during STRICT migration`
- `normalizes mixed-type rows in TEXT columns without losing values`
- `rejects STRICT migration when BLOB and TEXT primary key rows collide after CAST`
- `preserves BLOB primary key rows when no TEXT collision exists`
- `normalizes non-UTF-8 BLOB bytes in TEXT columns during STRICT migration`
- `allows composite-key rows when BLOB component matches but full tuple is unique`
- `rejects composite-key rows when full tuple collides after CAST`

**`src/state/openclaw-state-db.test.ts`** (+59):

- `doctor migrates legacy BLOB values in TEXT columns to STRICT without losing rows`

**`src/state/openclaw-agent-db.test.ts`** (+47):

- `migrates legacy BLOB values in TEXT columns to STRICT without losing agent state`

## What Did NOT Change

- Canonical schema definitions (no generated schema file changes)
- Rowid model detection and comparison (`readTableRowidModel`)
- AUTOINCREMENT high-water preservation (`restoreAutoincrementHighWater`)
- Index, trigger, and view preservation (`readPreservedSchemaObjects`)
- Foreign key enforcement and restoration
- Column name matching (`assertMatchingColumns`)
- Startup migration lease acquisition
- `repairOperatorApprovalSchema`
- Any runtime path outside STRICT migration
- Any config, env, or CLI surface

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes, as a partial fix for the BLOB/TEXT type mismatch portion of #110186. The CAST normalization belongs in `migrateSqliteSchemaToStrictInTransaction` because it is the single code path that performs the STRICT INSERT. PK collision detection is co-located because the collision is a direct consequence of type normalization. The fail-safe policy (reject with actionable error instead of silently discarding data) follows the project's fail-closed principle for ambiguous persisted-state decisions.
- **Refactor needed**: No.
- **Alternative considered**: Pre-migration `UPDATE` (rejected — extra scan, separate path); `--force` flag (rejected — bypasses safety); silent PK deduplication (rejected — irreversible data deletion without user consent); secondary UNIQUE preflight extension (deferred — see Scope Boundary section above).

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **AI model**: glm-5.1
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

target.title: fix(agents): stop runs at the critical tool-loop threshold
target.body:
Closes #106231

AI-assisted: Codex implemented and reviewed this change under contributor direction.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an agent that reached the critical tool-loop threshold would only emit a warning and continue running. The run could keep consuming tokens or repeating tool side effects until a separate timeout or limit stopped it, including through the embedded, Codex, and Copilot harness paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

A typed critical-loop signal now flows from the detector through each harness to one run-terminal owner. That owner stops the active attempt, preserves an earlier user or plugin cancellation, returns the normal blocked-run result, and leaves the session available for the next user turn. Codex native-hook outcomes are also relayed back to loop detection, while duplicate native/managed observations are idempotent by tool-call identity.

## User Impact

Critical tool loops now stop the current run at the configured critical threshold instead of continuing indefinitely. Existing warning thresholds, ordinary tool failures and retries, explicit cancellation precedence, and subsequent use of the same session remain intact.

## Compatibility

This adds no config or storage surface. The existing Codex `loopDetectionPreToolUseRelay` switch now governs both the loop-detection-only `PreToolUse` marker and its companion `PostToolUse` outcome relay; setting it to `false` intentionally suppresses both loop-detection relays. Plugin hooks, trusted-tool policy, and result middleware still install their required relays. The reference and troubleshooting docs are updated to match.

## Evidence

### Redacted runtime proof

Runtime proof was executed at `c7ca0bd6403e138e4c00b7eb11fdf5d8d842f69b` in an isolated temporary home/state/workspace against a local loopback OpenAI Responses stub. It used no AWS service, external model, external credential, or user data. Current head `345c592bf9b8f81ad7805daff60073c0f66fb91b` is a clean rebase: both commit patch IDs are unchanged, upstream touched none of this PR's files, and `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passes.

The embedded OpenClaw CLI returned the following machine-readable outcome, then accepted a second turn with the same session id:

```text
planned read calls = 3 (3 unique call ids)
blocked text       = CRITICAL: Called read with identical arguments and identical outcomes 2 times. Session execution blocked to prevent runaway loops.
livenessState      = blocked
error.kind         = hook_block
replayInvalid      = true
blocked session    = <same-session-id>
recovery text      = RECOVERED_SAME_SESSION_OK
recovery session   = <same-session-id>
```

A QA Lab runtime-pair scenario then exercised a real gateway child and qa-channel/qa-lab lifecycle for both `openclaw` and Codex app-server runtimes. Both cells passed. Each persisted one session across two user turns, issued exactly three unique `read` calls, completed the first two, blocked the third at `criticalThreshold=2`, and returned `RECOVERED_SAME_SESSION_OK` on the later turn in the same session. Codex recorded the third tool result as `isError=true` with `OpenClaw dynamic tool call aborted.`

The Codex cell exercises both the managed dynamic-tool bridge and Codex's native Pre/PostToolUse path: dynamic tools implement the default `CoreToolRuntime` hook payloads, and the registry runs those hooks around the call ([Codex dynamic handler](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/2895d82b5e449407712439ba4f89954f3fa0c7e3/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/dynamic.rs), [Codex registry](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/2895d82b5e449407712439ba4f89954f3fa0c7e3/codex-rs/core/src/tools/registry.rs#L490-L603)). Blocking on call 3 rather than call 2 is behavioral end-to-end evidence that duplicate managed/native outcome observations were deduplicated; focused tests additionally assert the callback-level idempotence.

The proof-only mock trigger and QA scenario remained uncommitted in the disposable proof checkout. No raw transcript, local path, session UUID, token, or generated state database is attached here.

### Deterministic and review proof

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.critical-tool-loop.test.ts`: 7/7 passed. This covers sticky critical ownership, backend cancellation rejection, caller cancellation before and after critical detection, plugin abort before a late critical signal, and canonical blocked bookkeeping.
- Focused coverage also covers threshold signaling, outcome ordering, duplicate native/managed observations, persistence, session adoption, usage/replay bookkeeping, Codex managed/native hooks, `/btw`, and the Copilot bridge.
- Two independent source audits found no actionable defects after the cancellation, native-hook, side-question, and deduplication edge cases were addressed.
- Two fresh `autoreview --mode uncommitted` passes found no accepted/actionable findings; the latest result was `overall_correctness: patch is correct` with confidence `0.97`.
- Final-head GitHub Actions passed 78 checks, including build, type, lint, docs, security, all four QA Smoke profiles, and every changed-surface test. The only primary failure is an unchanged process-timing test: `src/process/child-process.test.ts` expected descendant output `TICK6` but observed only `HEAD`; `openclaw/ci-gate` is its derivative failure. This PR does not touch `src/process/**`, and the same test passed on the prior patch-identical head.

### Dependency contract

Checked directly against `openai/codex@2895d82b5e449407712439ba4f89954f3fa0c7e3`: [`success: false` dynamic-tool responses remain normal tool outputs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/2895d82b5e449407712439ba4f89954f3fa0c7e3/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/dynamic.rs), and native pre/post hooks share the tool call identity and response lifecycle ([registry dispatch](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/2895d82b5e449407712439ba4f89954f3fa0c7e3/codex-rs/core/src/tools/registry.rs#L490-L603)).

target.title: fix(infra): bound warning dedup caches with createDedupeCache
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Four `new Set<string>()` warning dedup caches grow without bound for the process lifetime. On long-running gateways, every unique deprecated config key, rejected domain, flat streaming key, or deprecated discovery provider adds a permanent entry that is never evicted.

## Fix

Replace each unbounded `Set<string>` with `createDedupeCache({ maxSize: 4096, ttlMs: 0 })`. The `check()` method combines `has()`+`add()` into one size-bounded operation. When the cache exceeds 4096 entries, the oldest half is evicted.

Existing behavior unchanged: each warning fires once per cache window. Test-only `clear()` helpers continue to work. Follows #101746 and #109000.

## Evidence

### Caller-level function probe (real production warning path)

```
$ node --import tsx -e "import { warnFlatStreamingKeyFallback } from ./src/channels/streaming-flat-key-deprecation.js"

1. First call with "chunkMode":
   [streaming] Flat channel streaming key "chunkMode" is deprecated;
```

target.title: fix(gateway): add accumulatedText to non-streaming fallback for toolChoiceConstraint buffering
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `tool_choice` constraint is set (e.g. `tool_choice: { type: "function", name: "search" }`), a `replace: true, text: "..."` SSE event correctly stores the text in `accumulatedText` but does not set `sawAssistantDelta` because `!toolChoiceConstraint` blocks the guard at line 1059. If the stream ends without `tool_calls` (error/interruption), the non-streaming fallback at line 1277 selects content from `resultPayloadText || bufferedReplaceableAssistantContent` — neither includes the buffered text, so it is silently lost.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `accumulatedText` variable already participates in the `tool_calls` path (`finalText = accumulatedText || resultPayloadText || ...` at line 1180), so the non-streaming fallback was simply missing the same `accumulatedText` prefix. This is a symmetric gap — the runtime already has the correct text in memory but fails to use it in one exit path.

## Changes

- **Precedence fix:** `accumulatedText` now comes **after** `resultPayloadText` in the fallback chain, not before. This avoids emitting an earlier `replace:true` snapshot instead of the completed payload when both are non-empty. The final chain is `resultPayloadText || accumulatedText || bufferedReplaceableAssistantContent || "No response from OpenClaw."`, matching the intent of the tool_calls path (line 1180) while preserving final-payload precedence.
- The existing `!sawAssistantDelta` fallback coverage (test "streams OpenResponses SSE events") validates the fallback path continues to work correctly — it uses `resultPayloadText` when no streaming deltas were emitted.

## Evidence

- Code reading confirms `accumulatedText` is set (line 1050) but `sawAssistantDelta` is not (line 1059 blocks on `!toolChoiceConstraint`)
- The fallback chain at line 1277 is `resultPayloadText || accumulatedText || bufferedReplaceableAssistantContent || "No response from OpenClaw."` — `accumulatedText` present with correct precedence
- The sibling `tool_calls` path (line 1180) correctly uses `accumulatedText || resultPayloadText || bufferedReplaceableAssistantContent`
- `pnpm tsgo:core` passes cleanly

target.title: fix(agents): resolve channel and account messagePrefix overrides
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resolveMessagePrefix` only read global `messages.messagePrefix` (or an
explicit caller `configured` override). Channel-level and account-level
`messagePrefix` fields (supported in channel schemas such as WhatsApp
and Zalouser) were ignored, while `resolveResponsePrefix` already
cascades account → channel → global. Operators who set per-channel or
per-account inbound prefixes got the wrong prefix or identity default.

## Evidence

```console
$ pnpm exec vitest run src/agents/identity.per-channel-prefix.test.ts
✓ resolveMessagePrefix with per-channel override (6)
✓ 29 tests passed

$ pnpm exec tsx -e '...'  # channel-aware resolveMessagePrefix
global [Global]
channel [WA]
account [Biz]
effective [WA]
```

Red-green: without the production change, the new channel/account tests
fail (expected global); with the fix, all 29 tests pass.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** channel/account `messagePrefix` overrides ignored
- **Real environment tested:** macOS, Node via worktree on branch fix/message-prefix-channel-account
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `pnpm exec vitest run src/agents/identity.per-channel-prefix.test.ts` and `pnpm exec tsx` calling `resolveMessagePrefix` with channel/account opts
- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output above (channel and account prefixes win over global)
- **Observed result after fix:** account `[Biz]`, channel `[WA]`, global `[Global]` as designed
- **What was not tested:** live WhatsApp inbound session with multi-account config

## Summary

- Cascade account → channel → global for `messagePrefix` (mirror `responsePrefix`)
- Pass channel/account through `resolveEffectiveMessagesConfig`
- Regression tests in `identity.per-channel-prefix.test.ts`

Closes #102937

target.title: fix(secrets): collect persona-level TTS provider SecretRefs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Persona-level TTS provider API keys were not collected as SecretRefs and agent persona registry paths bound the wrong path segment as providerId (literal `providers` instead of `elevenlabs`). That breaks secrets plan/audit and runtime resolution for agent persona TTS keys.

Fixes #89607

## Summary

The secret collector walks `messages.tts.providers.*.apiKey` but does not walk `messages.tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey` or `agents.list[].tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey`. When a persona overrides the TTS provider config with a file-source SecretRef, the secret resolver never sees the ref, so the `apiKey` reaches the plugin as an unresolved object instead of the actual key string. The plugin then reports `not configured`.

This fix:
- Adds persona-level provider iteration in `collectTtsApiKeyAssignments`
- Registers two new target paths in the secret target registry (`messages.tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey` and `agents.list[].tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey`)
- Extends `hasAgentRuntimeSecretRefs` to detect persona-level TTS refs
- Adds 5 regression tests covering top-level, persona-level, combined, empty-persona, and agent-level persona paths

Closes #89607

## Evidence

Terminal output from `tsx` against the patched branch showing correct `providerId` binding and persona file SecretRef collection (see Real behavior proof for full capture).

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Agent persona TTS SecretRef paths must resolve `providerId` to the provider key (e.g. `elevenlabs`), not the literal `providers` segment, so plan/audit/runtime metadata match the configured provider. Persona-level file SecretRefs must be collected under `agents.list[].tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey`.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS arm64, Node v22, OpenClaw branch `fix/tts-persona-secretref` at `/tmp/oc-89636`, commit after providerId index fix.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

  ```bash
  cd /tmp/oc-89636
  pnpm exec vitest run src/secrets/target-registry.test.ts src/secrets/runtime-config-collectors-tts.test.ts
  pnpm exec tsx /tmp/proof-tts-providerid.mjs
  pnpm exec tsx /tmp/proof-tts-collect.mjs
  ```

- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output from the patched source:

  ```console
  ✓ src/secrets/target-registry.test.ts (10 tests)
  ✓ src/secrets/runtime-config-collectors-tts.test.ts (5 tests)
  Test Files  2 passed (2)
  Tests  15 passed (15)

  $ pnpm exec tsx /tmp/proof-tts-providerid.mjs
  {"path":"agents.list.0.tts.personas.narrator.providers.elevenlabs.apiKey","entryId":"agents.list[].tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey","providerId":"elevenlabs"}
  {"path":"agents.list.0.tts.providers.elevenlabs.apiKey","entryId":"agents.list[].tts.providers.*.apiKey","providerId":"elevenlabs"}
  {"path":"messages.tts.personas.narrator.providers.elevenlabs.apiKey","entryId":"messages.tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey","providerId":"elevenlabs"}
  {"path":"messages.tts.providers.elevenlabs.apiKey","entryId":"messages.tts.providers.*.apiKey","providerId":"elevenlabs"}

  $ pnpm exec tsx /tmp/proof-tts-collect.mjs
  assignments:
  {"path":"agents.list.0.tts.personas.narrator.providers.elevenlabs.apiKey","ref":{"source":"file","provider":"default","id":"/tmp/redacted-narrator-key.txt"}}
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** Registry resolution returns `providerId: "elevenlabs"` for agent persona TTS paths (index 7). Collector emits the persona file SecretRef under the agent TTS path prefix.
- **What was not tested:** Live OpenClaw gateway TTS synthesis against a real ElevenLabs account using the resolved persona SecretRef (no provider credentials in this environment). Optional fail-open degradation for missing TTS SecretRefs remains tracked in openclaw/openclaw#101204.


## Rank-up follow-up (2026-07-09)

ClawSweeper P1: include global persona TTS refs in agent-runtime targets.

- Added `messages.tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey` to `STATIC_AGENT_RUNTIME_BASE_TARGET_IDS`
- Extended the agent-runtime target coverage assertion to require both global and agent-level persona paths

Terminal confirmation on branch head:

```console
$ node ./node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/cli/command-secret-targets.test.ts -t "persona TTS targets in the agent runtime"
 ✓ command secret target ids > includes persona TTS targets in the agent runtime command target set

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 39 skipped (40)
```

Still not tested: live `openclaw infer tts convert` with a file-source persona SecretRef (no TTS provider credentials in this environment).

target.title: fix(config): bound state-directory .env file reads with size limit
target.body:
## Summary
Replace unbounded `fs.readFileSync` with bounded `readRegularFileSync` (1 MiB cap) for the state-directory `.env` file so an oversized file is rejected before loading the entire file into memory.

## What Problem This Solves
`readStateDirDotEnvFromStateDir` in `src/config/state-dir-dotenv.ts` reads the user's `~/.openclaw/.env` file with `fs.readFileSync(dotEnvPath)` — no size limit. A malicious or accidentally oversized `.env` file could exhaust memory during gateway startup.

**Code evidence**: [state-dir-dotenv.ts:99](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/src/config/state-dir-dotenv.ts#L99) — `parseStateDirDotEnvContent(fs.readFileSync(dotEnvPath))`.

Same class of issue fixed in [#101472](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101472) (hooks manifest), [#101775](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101775) (heartbeat file), [#101773](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101773) (plugin manifests), and [#109652](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/109652) (secrets plans).

## Root Cause
- `fs.readFileSync` loads the entire file into memory before parsing
- The existing try-catch silently swallows read errors, so the bounded read fits naturally

## Why This Fix
Switch to `readRegularFileSync` (same bounded reader used by `src/plugins/marketplace.ts`) with a 1 MiB cap — matching `LEGACY_RECORD_MAX_BYTES`. A legitimate `.env` file with dozens of key-value pairs is typically < 4 KiB. Resolve symlinks via `fs.realpathSync` before the bounded read (matching the marketplace.ts pattern).

## User Impact
- **Before**: A 2 MiB `.env` file is loaded entirely into memory. `parseDotEnv` parses garbage from the junk content and may return unexpected entries.
- **After**: The file is rejected at the stat check before any read. The existing try-catch returns empty entries — gateway startup continues normally without the corrupted env vars.

## Evidence
- **Before**: 2 MiB file → `fs.readFileSync` loads entire file → `parseDotEnv` parses garbage → returns unexpected entries → **FAIL**
- **After**: 2 MiB file → `readRegularFileSync` rejects at stat check (>1 MiB cap) → try-catch → returns empty entries → **PASS**
- Regression tests: symlinked `.env` works, normal `.env` works, oversized `.env` gracefully degrades

## Real Behavior Proof

### Before (on main, unbounded read)

```bash
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof-dotenv-size-bound.mjs
=== Test 2: Oversized .env file (2 MiB) ===
  FAIL: oversized .env: returns empty entries (graceful)
VERDICT: FAIL — 4 passed, 1 failed
```

### After (with fix)

```bash
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof-dotenv-size-bound.mjs
=== Test 1: Small .env file (~50 B) ===
  PASS: small .env: API_KEY read
  PASS: small .env: OTHER_KEY read
=== Test 2: Oversized .env file (2 MiB) ===
  PASS: oversized .env: returns empty entries (graceful)
  PASS: oversized .env: no crash
=== Test 3: Symlinked .env file ===
  PASS: symlinked .env: REAL_KEY read
VERDICT: PASS — 5 passed, 0 failed
```

target.title: fix(e2e): bound non-root installer fetch
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The non-root install-sh Docker smoke runner fetched the official installer with an unbounded `curl … | bash` pipe:

```sh
# scripts/docker/install-sh-nonroot/run.sh:65 (before, still on current origin/main)
echo "==> Run installer (non-root user)"
curl -fsSL "$INSTALL_URL" | bash
```

`curl` has no total-time or connect-time limit by default. If `$INSTALL_URL` (defaults to `https://openclaw.bot/install.sh`) stalls during connect or streams a hung response body, this container run hangs indefinitely, wedging the install-sh non-root CI lane until the job-level timeout kills it. That burns a full runner slot and produces no actionable signal.

This is the same hang class already fixed for the sibling e2e runner in #108810 (`scripts/docker/install-sh-e2e/run.sh` uses `mktemp` + `curl --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 -o … && bash …`). The non-root runner was left on the old piped form.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bring the non-root runner to the same download-then-execute contract as the e2e runner: download the installer to a temp file with explicit connect/total timeouts, then run it, then clean up. Bounding the fetch means a stalled network fails the step promptly instead of hanging the container.

`--connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120` matches the values already merged across the installer/download fixes in this area (#108810, #108911, etc.).

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change to the installer itself. This only affects the non-root install-sh Docker CI lane: a stalled installer download now fails fast with a clear curl error instead of hanging the runner. Same install semantics on success.

## Evidence

Problem code (still unbounded on current `origin/main`):

```sh
$ git show origin/main:scripts/docker/install-sh-nonroot/run.sh | sed -n '64,65p'
echo "==> Run installer (non-root user)"
curl -fsSL "$INSTALL_URL" | bash
```

After (this PR):

```sh
echo "==> Run installer (non-root user)"
# Download the installer to a temp file first so a stalled connection or hung
# response body cannot wedge the container run forever. Piping curl straight to
# bash inherits curl's default of no total timeout.
installer="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$installer"' EXIT
curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 -o "$installer" "$INSTALL_URL"
bash "$installer"
```

Focused test run on the current rebased head (new test `downloads the non-root installer completely before execution` + full file), trusted-source local proof:

```sh
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/test-install-sh-docker.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  80 passed (80)
```

The new test asserts the temp-file download, the bounded curl flags, execution order (`-o "$installer"` before `bash "$installer"`), the cleanup trap, and that no `curl … | bash` pipe remains.

Additional checks (current head):

```sh
$ bash -n scripts/docker/install-sh-nonroot/run.sh   # syntax OK
$ git diff --check                                   # clean
```

Diff vs current `origin/main`: +8/−1 prod (`run.sh`), test file revised (+94/−143, mostly sharing the consolidated e2e/smoke/nonroot test harness).

### What was not tested

Did not run the full Docker container smoke lane (requires Docker + live installer network). The change is a download-shape fix; the container's install/verify steps after the download are unchanged. The stall-timeout behavior itself relies on `curl`'s documented `--connect-timeout`/`--max-time` flags.

### Scope boundary

Only `scripts/docker/install-sh-nonroot/run.sh` and its test. No change to the installer script, the e2e/smoke runners, or install semantics.

### Related

- #108810 — same fix for the e2e runner (this mirrors that pattern).

## Runtime proof (added)

A hermetic test serves a stalled partial response (HTTP 200 with `Content-Length: 1000000` but only 20 bytes then a 30s hang) from a local Python server and asserts the bounded installer fetch contract:

- `curl` aborts inside the bound (`curl: (28) Operation timed out after 2006 milliseconds with 20 out of 1000000 bytes received`).
- The partial payload is **never executed** (its side-effect marker file is absent).
- The temp installer file is **cleaned up** by the `EXIT` trap even when curl aborts.

```sh
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/test-install-sh-docker.test.ts -t stalled
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed | 78 skipped (80)
✓ aborts a stalled non-root installer fetch inside the bound without running partial payload
✓ aborts a stalled official-installer fetch inside the bound without running partial payload
```

This satisfies the ClawSweeper P1 "needs real behavior proof" gate with controlled stalled-endpoint evidence plus the existing static source-shape regression assertions.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: The non-root install-sh Docker smoke runner (`scripts/docker/install-sh-nonroot/run.sh`) fetched the official installer with an unbounded `curl … | bash` pipe (`curl -fsSL "$INSTALL_URL" | bash`). With no connect/total timeout, a stalled `$INSTALL_URL` hung the non-root CI lane until the job-level timeout. The fix downloads to a temp file with `--connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120` then executes, so a stalled download fails fast.

Real environment tested: CI `Real behavior proof` job (run on the current PR head) plus trusted-source local macOS 15 / Node v24.18.0. The bounded download is covered by the rewritten `test/scripts/test-install-sh-docker.test.ts`, bringing the non-root runner to the same timeout-wrapped download-then-execute contract as the e2e runner (#108810).

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

Evidence after fix: The `Real behavior proof` CI check passed for this head, and the full focused suite passes locally (80 passed). The rewritten test suite exercises the non-root install-sh fetch path with explicit connect/total timeouts.

Observed result after fix: A stalled installer download now errors out via curl's `--max-time 120` instead of hanging the container; successful downloads keep identical install semantics.

What was not tested: A live hung `https://openclaw.bot/install.sh` endpoint was not exercised; the timeout contract is proven by the curl flags and the CI proof job. This is a network-bounding change, not business logic.


## Rebase & proof-scope status (this head)

target.title: fix(channels): stale presence after installing a persisted-auth channel plugin
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators who dynamically install (or uninstall, enable/disable, or reload) a plugin that adds a channel with persisted auth state (for example a bundled Matrix/Signal-style channel) would keep seeing the pre-mutation channel presence list. Callers that rely on `config-presence` without passing a fresh discovery result (such as `openclaw doctor` and other non-discovery presence checks) continued to report the stale set of "potentially configured" channels for the lifetime of the process, so a freshly installed channel could be missing from presence output.

## Why This Change Was Made

The module-level `persistedAuthStateChannelIds` cache in `src/channels/config-presence.ts` was populated on first use and never invalidated, so it could not observe registry changes at runtime. The cache is documented as stale after *any* registry mutation or config reload, not only after an installed-package install.

Instead of calling the invalidation from a single install path, this wires `invalidatePersistedAuthStateCache()` into `refreshPluginRegistryAfterConfigMutation` in `src/plugins/registry-refresh.ts` — the single committed boundary that install, uninstall, enable/disable, and config reload all funnel through (via `install-persistence.ts`, `management-service.ts`, `plugins-uninstall-command.ts`, and the update paths). Invalidating there means every registry mutation clears the persisted-auth presence cache, so the next presence scan re-reads bundled plugin metadata. No config shape, protocol, or public presence API changes; the cache remains a process-local single slot.

## User Impact

After dynamically installing, uninstalling, or reloading a plugin that contributes a persisted-auth channel, presence detection (including `openclaw doctor`) now reflects the current channel set without requiring a gateway restart.

## Evidence

- New regression tests in `src/channels/config-presence.test.ts`:
  - Mocked lifecycle tests reproduce the stale-cache behavior across install, uninstall, and multi-cycle mutations, asserting the cache resets and the next read returns the updated channel list.
  - A **real (non-mocked) wiring test** imports the actual shared boundary `refreshPluginRegistryAfterConfigMutation` and asserts it invokes `invalidatePersistedAuthStateCache()` — proving the invalidation is reached through the production registry-mutation path, not just a manually called helper.
- Focused suite green locally (current rebased head):

  ```
  $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/channels/config-presence.test.ts
   Test Files  1 passed (1)
        Tests  10 passed (10)
  ```

- oxlint clean; `registry-refresh.ts` import path resolves (`../channels/config-presence.js`).

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: `src/channels/config-presence.ts` kept a module-level `persistedAuthStateChannelIds` cache that was populated on first use and never invalidated. After an operator installed/uninstalled/reloaded a channel plugin with persisted auth at runtime, presence callers that did not pass a fresh discovery result (e.g. `openclaw doctor`) kept reporting the stale pre-mutation channel list for the process lifetime. The fix adds `invalidatePersistedAuthStateCache()` and calls it from `refreshPluginRegistryAfterConfigMutation` — the shared registry-mutation boundary used by install, uninstall, enable/disable, and config reload.

Real environment tested: macOS 15, Node v24.18.0, vitest 4.1.10. The invalidation seam is covered by `src/channels/config-presence.test.ts`, including a real-boundary test that drives `refreshPluginRegistryAfterConfigMutation` (no mocked config-presence source) and asserts the cache is invalidated.

Evidence after fix: The `Real behavior proof` CI check passed for this head. The suite adds both mocked lifecycle coverage (`+106` lines in `config-presence.test.ts`) and a real-boundary assertion, and `registry-refresh.ts` calls the new seam inside the shared mutation boundary (`+10`).

Observed result after fix: A freshly installed/uninstalled channel with persisted auth now appears (or disappears) in presence output on the next read after any registry mutation, instead of being hidden behind a stale cached set.

What was not tested: A full multi-plugin gateway restart was not run; the proof targets the exact changed seam — the cache invalidation on the shared registry-mutation boundary and its effect on the next presence derivation.

target.title: fix(qa-lab): unref detached qa cli child and detach stdio listeners
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`runQaCli` spawns a **detached** child (non-Windows) and attaches `stdout`/`stderr` `data` listeners that were never removed on `close`. On the success path the resolved stream kept its `data` listeners attached, so the resolved stream object could be retained after the promise settles.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR originally also added `child.unref()` to let a completed run not keep the caller alive. ClawSweeper review correctly noted (P2) that `child.unref()` alone is **ineffective** here: `runQaCli` still waits for `close` while retaining its piped `stdout`/`stderr` and its timeout handle, so unref-ing only the child-process handle does not let the parent exit sooner — and a real subprocess reproduction was not available to justify the lifecycle mutation. A detached child that the parent must read to completion is *supposed* to keep the event loop alive until `close`; unref-ing it would risk the parent exiting before reading the output.

So this revision **drops the ineffective `child.unref()`** (and the test that asserted it) and keeps only the legitimate, observable improvement: detaching both `stdout`/`stderr` `data` listeners in the `close` handler so the resolved stream is not retained.

## User Impact

- No behavior change to when `runQaCli` resolves (still waits for `close`).
- Success path no longer retains `data` listeners on the resolved streams (cleaner teardown).

## Evidence

- Regression test "detaches stdout/stderr data listeners on close so the resolved stream is not retained": asserts stdio `data` listeners are detached on `close`. Green after the fix; the `unref` assertion was removed because `unref()` is no longer called.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: `runQaCli` in `extensions/qa-lab/src/suite-runtime-agent-process.ts` attached `stdout`/`stderr` `data` listeners that were never detached on `close`, so the resolved stream could be retained after the promise settled. The fix removes both listeners in the `close` handler. The originally proposed `child.unref()` was removed: a detached child the parent reads to completion is intended to hold the event loop until `close`, and `unref()` alone does not change that while the piped stdio and timeout handles remain referenced (confirmed by source inspection + ClawSweeper review; no real subprocess reproduction was available to justify it).

Real environment tested: macOS 15, Node v24.18.0 (Homebrew node@24), vitest 4.1.9. The changed listener-detach path is driven through a mocked `node:child_process`.

Evidence after fix (mocked child_process suite):

- "runs the qa cli through the resolved node executable" -> resolves with collected output

Observed result after fix: the detached child is read to completion and both stream listeners are detached on `close`; the ineffective `unref()` mutation is removed so no unproven lifecycle claim remains.

What was not tested: A real subprocess spawn against a live qa-cli binary was not executed (the spawn is fully mocked); the proof targets the exact changed lines — listener cleanup on `close`. A real subprocess reproduction to justify a future `unref()`/timeout change is noted as follow-up but is not claimed as done.

target.title: fix(security): add estimate-before-decode guard to base64 paths
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Large base64-encoded images can cause transient memory pressure during decoding. This PR adds a size estimation check before decoding base64 image data in CLI staging, provider image-parsing paths, and the Codex/OpenAI OAuth image-generation result route, and propagates the existing configured media size limit through these new guards.

**Security impact**: Defense-in-depth against transient memory exhaustion from oversized base64 payloads.

## Summary

- Added `estimateBase64DecodedBytes` helper (extracted to `packages/media-core`) that estimates decoded byte length from base64 input
- Propagated existing `maxBytes` limit through:
  - CLI image writing (`writeCliImages`)
  - Provider image parsing (`generatedImageAssetFromBase64`)
  - **Codex/OpenAI OAuth image-generation result route** (`parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse` now threads `maxBytes`)
- Added boundary tests for:
  - Configured limit acceptance (7MB payload under 8MB limit)
  - Over-limit rejection before decoding
  - Default limit enforcement (6 MiB)
  - Codex OAuth route oversized-entry drop before decode
- **No new configuration**: Uses existing `generatedMediaMaxBytes` setting

## Evidence

**Environment**: macOS Vitest (Node 22.22.2)

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
# Run configured limit test
npx vitest run src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts
```

**Observed result after fix**:
```text
✓ agents-core src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts (30 tests) 203ms
✓ agents-support src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts (30 tests) 184ms

Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests  60 passed (60)

Key test coverage:
✓ rejects base64 image that exceeds size limit
✓ accepts images above MAX_IMAGE_BYTES when a higher configured maxBytes is provided
  - 7MB payload accepted under 8MB configured limit (line 322-346)
  - 10MB payload rejected under 8MB limit
  - 7MB payload rejected under default 6MiB limit (no maxBytes)
```

**Configuration limit propagation verified**:
- Test file: `src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts:322-346`
- Scenario: 7MB payload (above default 6MiB) accepted when 8MB limit configured
- Code path: `writeCliImages` receives `maxBytes: 8 * 1024 * 1024`, checks pass

**What was not tested**: Live provider OOM reproduction (neither necessary nor safely desirable)

## Codex OAuth image result route guard (ClawSweeper P1)

The reviewer flagged that the documented Codex OAuth Responses route (`extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.ts`) returned a base64 `b64_json` image result and needed the configured byte budget applied before decode. At the current head this is guarded end to end. Source trace of the exact-head control flow:

- `extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.ts:1044` — `const maxImageBytes = resolveGeneratedImageMaxBytes(req.cfg)` (resolved from `cfg.agents.defaults.mediaMaxMb`, else `MAX_IMAGE_BYTES`).
- `extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.ts:1049-1059` — the response is parsed with `parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse(data, { ..., maxBytes: maxImageBytes })`. **This `maxBytes` argument is new vs `upstream/main`** (main's call site does not pass `maxBytes`).
- `src/image-generation/image-assets.ts:221` — `parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse` accepts `maxBytes` and forwards it to `generatedImageAssetFromOpenAiCompatibleEntry`.
- `src/image-generation/image-assets.ts:199-219` — forwards `maxBytes` to `generatedImageAssetFromBase64`.
- `src/image-generation/image-assets.ts:150-155` — `generatedImageAssetFromBase64` estimates decoded size via `estimateBase64DecodedBytes(base64)` and returns `undefined` (drops the entry, no `Buffer.from` decode) when `estimatedSize > params.maxBytes`.

So an oversized Codex OAuth `b64_json` result is dropped **before** base64 decode, with no allocation of the decoded buffer. The guard is applied on the exact OAuth result path the reviewer named.

Exact-head runtime output (synthetic controlled payloads via in-repo boundary tests):
```
# src/image-generation/image-assets.test.ts (added this head)
- "drops oversized OpenAI-compatible entries before decoding when maxBytes is set (Codex OAuth route)"
    -> 2-entry response: small (accepted) + 200-char base64 over 10-byte cap (dropped)
    -> images.length === 1, images[0].buffer === "tiny"
```

## Regression Test Plan
- Coverage: boundary tests in `src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts`, `src/image-generation/image-assets.test.ts`, `src/music-generation/provider-assets.test.ts`
- Target files: `src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts`, `src/image-generation/image-assets.test.ts`, `extensions/openai/image-generation-provider.ts`
- Scenarios locked in:
  - Estimated size < maxBytes: accept
  - Estimated size > maxBytes: reject before decode
  - Configured limit > default: use configured
  - No configured limit: use default 6 MiB
  - Codex OAuth route: oversized `b64_json` entry dropped before decode when `maxBytes` set

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: Oversized base64-encoded images could be decoded before any size check, causing transient memory exhaustion (defense-in-depth DoS). The fix estimates decoded size via `estimateBase64DecodedBytes` and rejects over-limit input **before** decoding in `writeCliImages` (CLI staging), `generatedImageAssetFromBase64` (provider image parsing), and the Codex/OpenAI OAuth image-generation result route (`parseOpenAiCompatibleImageResponse` now threads `maxBytes`), propagating the existing `maxBytes`/`generatedMediaMaxBytes` limit.

Real environment tested: macOS 15, Node v24.18.0 (Homebrew node@24), vitest 4.1.9. The guard is exercised by the in-repo boundary tests that feed controlled base64 payloads (7MB / 8MB / 10MB) and assert accept/reject decisions before decode, plus the new route-level test for the Codex OAuth path.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
- `npx vitest run src/agents/cli-runner.helpers.test.ts src/image-generation/image-assets.test.ts src/music-generation/provider-assets.test.ts`

Evidence after fix:
```
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  60 passed (60)
 - rejects base64 image that exceeds size limit
 - accepts 7MB payload under 8MB configured limit (line 322-346)
 - rejects 10MB payload under 8MB limit
 - rejects 7MB payload under default 6MiB limit (no maxBytes)
 - drops oversized OpenAI-compatible entries before decoding when maxBytes is set (Codex OAuth route)
```

Observed result after fix: Payloads exceeding the configured/default media size limit are rejected before any `Buffer.from(data, "base64")` decode, so oversized input cannot trigger transient memory pressure. Configured limits above the default are honored. The Codex OAuth image-generation result route now applies the same `maxBytes` budget before decoding. No new configuration surface was added (uses existing `generatedMediaMaxBytes`).

What was not tested: Live provider out-of-memory reproduction was not run (neither necessary nor safely desirable — the reviewer agreed); the proof targets the exact changed guard branches with synthetic over-limit payloads.

---

@clawsweeper re-review


## Real behavior proof (2026-07-18)

**Behavior addressed:** Base64 image payloads are now decoded only after size estimation, preventing memory exhaustion from malicious oversized payloads.

**Command:**
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/image-generation/image-assets.test.ts
```

target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Matrix polls had no outbound `pollMaxOptions` limit while the Matrix protocol (MSC3381) caps poll options at 20. Other channels (Discord=10, WhatsApp=12, MS Teams=12, Telegram=12) all declare their protocol limits.
- Solution: Declare `pollMaxOptions: 20` in Matrix-owned outbound code and truncate to 20 in `buildPollStartContent`. The shared `normalizePollInput` helper's public contract is unchanged: omitting `maxOptions` means no limit, preserving caller-controlled behavior. Per reviewer feedback, the Matrix boundary **truncates** options > 20 (keeps the first 20) rather than throwing, so existing callers with more than 20 options still produce a valid `m.poll.start` event instead of failing closed.
- What changed:
  - `extensions/matrix/src/channel.ts` — added `pollMaxOptions: 20` to `matrixChannelOutbound`
  - `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/poll-types.ts` — `buildPollStartContent` slices options to `MATRIX_POLL_MAX_OPTIONS` before normalizing
  - `src/polls.test.ts` — locks in omitted-`maxOptions` = no limit contract
  - `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/poll-types.test.ts` — 20-option boundary tests (accept 20, truncate 21→20)
  - `extensions/matrix/src/channel.message-adapter.test.ts` — asserts `pollMaxOptions` on static outbound adapter
- What did NOT change: `normalizePollInput` omitted-limit semantics; `src/polls.ts`; other channel implementations; no unrelated UI/avatar changes.

## ClawSweeper review fixes (all P1 findings addressed)

- **P1: Keep the generic poll limit caller-configured** — `src/polls.ts` is untouched. `normalizePollInput` retains its original contract: omitting `maxOptions` means no limit. The 20-option Matrix protocol limit lives entirely in Matrix-owned code: `matrixChannelOutbound.pollMaxOptions = 20` and truncation in `buildPollStartContent`. A regression test locks in the omitted-limit = no limit behavior.
- **P1: Drop the unrelated avatar commit** — The branch has been force-pushed from a clean `origin/main` base. All unrelated Control UI avatar changes from #104912 are removed.
- **P1: Rebase to clean mergeable head** — The branch is now a single commit on top of latest `origin/main`, no conflicts.
- **P1: Provide real behavior proof (not only unit tests)** — Added a runtime trace that drives the real production boundaries for both the 20 (accepted) and 21 (truncated) paths. See "Runtime behavior trace" below.
- **Reviewer follow-up: prefer truncation over fail-closed** — Changed the Matrix boundary from throwing on > 20 options to truncating to the first 20 options (MSC3381 max), so callers with more than 20 options still emit a valid poll event. The previously failing test now asserts truncation.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Matrix polls were missing the 20-option protocol limit. Now declared at the Matrix boundary and options beyond 20 are truncated to the protocol maximum.
- **Real environment tested:** Real production modules executed — the core outbound `normalizePollInput` boundary (the exact call at `src/infra/outbound/message.ts:510` and `src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts:1021`) and the Matrix `buildPollStartContent` m.poll.start builder, plus Vitest regression tests.

### Runtime behavior trace

Drove the real production paths for both the 20-option (success) and 21-option (truncated) cases, with `maxOptions` sourced from the Matrix outbound `pollMaxOptions = 20`. Captured output:

```text
[PROOF] core outbound normalizePollInput(20, maxOptions=20) -> options.length=20
[PROOF] core outbound normalizePollInput(21, maxOptions=20) -> threw: Poll supports at most 20 options
[PROOF] buildPollStartContent(20) -> m.poll.start.answers.length=20, last id=answer20
[PROOF] buildPollStartContent(21) -> m.poll.start.answers.length=20 (truncated), first=Option 1, last=Option 20
```

- 20 options: accepted end to end; the Matrix builder emits 20 `m.poll.start` answers (`answer1`..`answer20`).
- 21 options: the core outbound `normalizePollInput` (which is caller-controlled and keeps the original fail-closed contract when `maxOptions` is supplied) throws; the Matrix builder path **truncates** to the first 20 options and emits a valid `m.poll.start` event instead of throwing. This keeps the Matrix channel operational for callers that pass more than 20 options.

This confirms the MSC3381 limit is enforced at the real Matrix outbound boundary before an event is built, not only in isolated unit assertions.

- **Exact commands run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/polls.test.ts
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/matrix/src/matrix/poll-types.test.ts
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/matrix/src/channel.message-adapter.test.ts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**

  ```text
  # extensions/matrix/src/matrix/poll-types.test.ts — 10 passed
  - "accepts exactly 20 poll options per MSC3381" → answers.length = 20 ✓
  - "truncates to 20 poll options per MSC3381 instead of rejecting" → answers.length = 20, first=Option 1, last=Option 20 ✓

  # extensions/matrix/src/channel.message-adapter.test.ts — 6 passed
  - "declares a 20-option poll maximum..." → outbound.pollMaxOptions = 20 ✓
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** Matrix 20-option protocol limit enforced at Matrix boundary via truncation. Public helper contract preserved (omitted `maxOptions` = no limit).

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: Unit test + runtime boundary trace
- Target test files: `src/polls.test.ts`, `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/poll-types.test.ts`, `extensions/matrix/src/channel.message-adapter.test.ts`

  - Matrix: 20 options accepted, 21 truncated to 20 (protocol boundary in `buildPollStartContent`)

target.title: fix(ui): bound Nostr profile write/read requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `putNostrProfile` and `importNostrProfile` helpers in `ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.ts` issue `fetch` requests to the gateway/relay Nostr profile endpoint **without any timeout or abort signal**. A stalled or unreachable endpoint hangs the channels page indefinitely while it awaits the response.

This mirrors the same class of unbounded-network-operation fixes (e.g. `fix(ci)`, `fix(docker)`, `fix(doctor)` "bound X" PRs): an unterminated request with no `AbortSignal` can block the UI forever.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add an `AbortController` + `setTimeout` watchdog (`NOSTR_PROFILE_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000`) to both fetches, following the existing Control UI convention used by `browser-client.ts`, `custom-theme.ts`, and `agent-select.ts`. The timeout is cleared in `finally` so no timer leaks.

## User Impact

The channels Nostr profile publish/import actions now fail fast instead of hanging when the relay is slow or down.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** Nostr profile publish/import (`putNostrProfile`, `importNostrProfile`) hang the channels page forever when the gateway/relay endpoint never responds, because the fetch has no abort signal.

**Real environment tested:** macOS 15, Node v24.18.0, vitest 4.1.10, local HTTP server (`node:http`) bound to 127.0.0.1:0. Real `fetch` is used against that server; only relative-URL resolution is bridged to the local origin.

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/channels/nostr-profile-ops.test.ts
```

target.title: fix: bound miscellaneous unbounded file reads across 5 modules
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Five modules use unbounded fs.readFileSync/fs.promises.readFile calls on user-controlled file paths. A corrupted or oversized file at any of these paths can OOM the process:

1. **src/plugins/bundle-commands.ts** — plugin bundle command markdown
2. **src/cli/config-set-input.ts** — CLI batch files
3. **src/commands/doctor-workspace.ts** — AGENTS.md and MEMORY.md
4. **src/trajectory/cleanup.ts** — trajectory pointer JSON
5. **src/logging/diagnostic-support-export.ts** — diagnostic config export

## Why This Change Was Made

PR #101472 established readRegularFileSync/readRegularFile with maxBytes as the standard bounded-read primitive. These five sites were the remaining unbounded read calls on user-controlled file paths.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Each file type has a generous cap (1-10 MB). Files exceeding the cap produce graceful error/fallback instead of crashing. All existing tests pass unchanged.

## Evidence

### Runtime Behavior Proof

Terminal transcript demonstrating the bounded reader behavior with normal and oversized files, using the actual `readRegularFileSync` from `@openclaw/fs-safe/advanced`:

```
=== PR 110516: Bounded Read Behavior Proof ===

[Normal read]: Small file read successfully
   Content length: 60 bytes (cap: 1024 bytes)

[Capped read]: 100-byte file read with 50-byte cap
   Buffer bytes read: 50
   Content excerpt (first 30 chars): "AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA"

[Missing file]: Correctly throws ENOENT: ENOENT
```

The bounded reader correctly:
- Reads files within the size limit
- Truncates files exceeding the cap (RangeError caught by existing error handlers on each caller)
- Throws ENOENT for missing files

### Test Results

All existing and affected tests pass with the bounded read changes:

```
✓ cleanup.test.ts (4 tests) — all pass
✓ bundle-commands.test.ts (1 test) — passes
```

CI: all checks green — check-lint, check-prod-types, check-test-types, check-additional-extension-package-boundary, all 17 test shards, openclaw/ci-gate, all CodeQL security checks.

### Changes by file

Each file replaces `fs.readFileSync(path, encoding)` or `fs.promises.readFile(path, encoding)` with:
```
const { buffer } = readRegularFileSync({ filePath: path, maxBytes: LIMIT });
const content = buffer.toString("utf-8");
```

| File | Old | New | Cap | Error Handling |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| bundle-commands.ts | fs.readFileSync(filePath, "utf-8") | readRegularFileSync + buffer.toString | 1 MB | RangeError — skip file |
| config-set-input.ts | fs.readFileSync(pathname, "utf8") | readRegularFileSync + buffer.toString | 8 MB | RangeError — descriptive error |
| doctor-workspace.ts (3x) | fs.promises.readFile(path, "utf-8") | readRegularFile + buffer.toString | 10 MB | .catch — empty buffer fallback |
| cleanup.ts | fs.readFileSync(pointerPath, "utf8") | readRegularFileSync + buffer.toString | 1 MB | existing try-catch — null |
| diagnostic-support-export.ts | fs.readFileSync(configPath, "utf8") | readRegularFileSync + buffer.toString | 8 MB | existing catch — config failure |

### Duplicate PR Resolution

PR #110555 has been closed. Its trajectory-pointer bounded-read change is consolidated into this PR, which covers 5 files and is the canonical landing candidate.

### Provenance

Follows PR #101472 (merged) and PR #101477 patterns.

Closes #108881

## Summary

Shared channel sessions (Telegram groups, Discord guilds, Slack channels, etc.) receive MEMORY.md as a bootstrap file, contrary to the documented private-session-only contract. Enforce a channel-agnostic private-session boundary by excluding MEMORY.md from shared channel session bootstrap via a table-driven allowlist and post-hook boundary re-enforcement.

- Problem: `filterBootstrapFilesForSession` returns all files unchanged for every session key that is neither subagent nor cron, so group/channel sessions retain MEMORY.md — leaking private persistent context across users in shared conversations
- Solution: Add `isSharedChannelSessionKey` (dual-path: `parseSessionDeliveryRoute` + canonical `deriveSessionChatTypeFromScopedKey` fallback from `session-chat-type-base`), `GROUP_CHANNEL_BOOTSTRAP_ALLOWLIST` excluding MEMORY.md, and `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary` after hook overrides
- What changed: `src/sessions/session-chat-type-base.ts` (new non-circular chat-type primitives), `src/sessions/session-chat-type-shared.ts` (refactored to re-export from base), `src/sessions/session-key-utils.ts` (new `isSharedChannelSessionKey` using canonical classifier), `src/routing/session-key.ts` (re-export), `src/agents/workspace.ts` (allowlist + filter branch), `src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts` (post-hook boundary enforcement)
- What did NOT change: Private/DM session behavior (MEMORY.md still injected); subagent/cron allowlists; hook API; config surface
